magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is partially aligned with Catholic teaching because it grieves for every victim and describes the conflict as unnecessary and bloody, but the available excerpt does not show a clear condemnation of forced expulsion nor the protection of civilians as a moral principle. The claims about directing displaced persons may be historically and politically relevant, but in themselves they do not clarify responsibility for their suffering nor the moral impermissibility of forced transfers.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Church teaching recognizes displaced persons as persons whose dignity and needs require protection, and Sacred Scripture repeatedly speaks of flight and exile, including the flight of the Holy Family into Egypt. Therefore, the Catholic evaluation of war does not stop at grieving for victims: it demands the protection of the innocent, respect for humanitarian law, and the condemnation of forced expulsion, regardless of which side the perpetrators or victims belong to.
concerns_en: The expression that the Serbs directed displaced persons "very deliberately" attributes intent to a group, but the excerpt does not provide support for that claim; its historical accuracy cannot be assessed from the provided text alone.

Catholic teaching explicitly rejects forced transfers of populations under the guise of ethnic cleansing and demands the protection of innocent civilians, so a clear distinction should be made between describing the military-political context and justifying or diminishing responsibility for atrocities.

sections.subtitle_en: Lašvanska dolina: twelve months in an encirclement in which "not even a bird could come"
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest quotes American officer Charles Shrader on the encirclement of Croats in Lašvanska dolina
sections.content_en:
Kordić describes to listeners who are less familiar with the circumstances the HVO operational zone in central Bosnia. It encompassed Žepče, Usora, Kakanj, Vareš, Zenica, Lepenička dolina with Kiseljak, Kreševo, and Fojnica, then **Lašvanska dolina**, Vrbaska dolina with Jajce and Bugojno, and Uskoplje up to Kupres.

Regarding the cause of the conflict between Muslims and Croats, which he calls unnecessary and bloody, he says that everyone is sorry for every victim. Still, he claims one needs to be realistic. According to his words, the Serbs cleansed the largest part of the area and "very deliberately" directed the displaced persons toward central Bosnia. Croatian displaced persons mostly went toward Croatia or to the West, while Muslim displaced persons remained in Travnik, Bugojno, and other places where the population had until then been "half-and-half". Instead of encouraging them to return to the areas lost to the Serbs, someone, he says, told them: "This is your El Dorado now… you only need to conquer it from a softer opponent." That is how, according to his interpretation, the aggression against the Croats began.

He refers to **Charles Shrader**, a senior American officer who testified at his trial and wrote a book about the war in central Bosnia. Shrader, according to Kordić, said: "Do not speak nonsense that Croats from Lašvanska dolina can attack anyone when they are in total encirclement." The encirclement lasted almost twelve months and encompassed Busovača, Vitez, Novi Travnik, and Nova Bila. In Nova Bila, a Franciscan hospital operated where the wounded were treated in church pews.

The casualties were immense. Vitez had about 12,000 residents according to the census and not all remained during the war, and there, according to Kordić, around **700 people** were killed. In Busovača, around 250 were killed. He also mentions the Travnik cemetery Prahulje full of Croatian defenders, the brigade Ban Jelačić from Kiseljak, as well as Žepče, Jajce, Bugojno, and Uskoplje: "Everyone had their own story."

sections.subtitle: Krunica oko vrata svakog branitelja
sections.screenshot_description: Kordić govori o krunici kao izvoru snage pod granatama
sections.content:
Usred priče o ratnim stradanjima Kordić ističe ono što smatra presudnim. Vojnici i političari mogli su činiti sve što su mogli, ali su majke, očevi, bake, djedovi, supruge i djeca pod granatama, skrivajući se u skloništima, **molili krunicu**.

„Ta krunica je davala snagu i bila je oko vrata svakog hrvatskog branitelja“, kaže. Kao jednako važne ističe i svećenike koji su ostali s narodom. Sve to naziva sudbonosnim.

Zaključuje da je Gospodin htio da Hrvati ostanu „na ostacima ostataka“. Nisu se održali na svakom dijelu prostora, ali Kordić zahvaljuje Bogu što su opstali u središnjoj Bosni, **„u nadi protiv svake nade“**.

magisterium.assessment: Isticanje molitve krunice i svećenika koji ostaju uz ljude u nevolji uglavnom je u skladu s katoličkim razumijevanjem molitve kao oslonca u trpljenju, a ne jamstva tjelesne sigurnosti; ona vjerniku može dati snagu da u kušnji ostane uz Boga. Izjava da je Gospodin htio da Hrvati opstanu može se razumjeti kao pouzdanje u Božju providnost, ali bez dodatnog pojašnjenja riskira da određeni povijesni ishod predstavi kao nedvojbeno poznatu Božju namjeru.
concerns: Tvrdnju o Božjoj volji za opstanak određenog naroda valja iznositi ponizno: vjera u providnost ne znači da možemo sa sigurnošću proglasiti konkretan ratni ishod izravnim znakom Božje naklonosti ili potvrdom političkog cilja.
Izraz „oko vrata svakog hrvatskog branitelja” u prikazanom odlomku djeluje kao retoričko uopćavanje, a ne doslovna tvrdnja koju je moguće teološki procijeniti.
magisterium.enrichment: Kršćanska molitva nije zaštitni amulet niti obećanje da će vjernik izbjeći ranjavanje i smrt; njezin plod može biti pouzdanje u Boga i snaga da se u kušnji ne odrekne dobra. Govor o „ostatku” može odjekivati biblijskom slikom naroda koji je sačuvan kroz nevolju, no tu sliku treba primjenjivati pažljivo i bez zaključka da su patnja ili opstanak sami po sebi dokaz Božjeg odobravanja svih postupaka neke strane.
magisterium.assessment_en: Emphasizing the prayer of the Rosary and priests who remain with the people in distress is largely in accordance with the Catholic understanding of prayer as a support in suffering, rather than a guarantee of bodily safety; it can give the believer the strength to remain with God in trial. The statement that the Lord wanted the Croats to survive can be understood as trust in God's providence, but without additional clarification it risks presenting a specific historical outcome as an undoubtedly known intention of God.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Christian prayer is not a protective amulet nor a promise that a believer will avoid injury and death; its fruit can be trust in God and strength not to renounce the good in trial. Speaking of the "remnant" may echo the biblical image of a people preserved through adversity, but that image should be applied carefully and without the conclusion that suffering or survival are in themselves proof of God's approval of all actions of one side.
concerns_en: The claim about God's will for the survival of a specific nation should be stated humbly: faith in providence does not mean that we can proclaim with certainty a concrete wartime outcome as a direct sign of God's favor or a confirmation of a political goal.
The expression "around the neck of every Croatian defender" in the presented passage appears as a rhetorical generalization, rather than a literal claim that can be evaluated theologically.

sections.subtitle_en: A Rosary around the neck of every defender
sections.screenshot_description_en: Kordić speaks about the Rosary as a source of strength under artillery shells
sections.content_en:
In the midst of the story about wartime suffering, Kordić emphasizes what he considers crucial. Soldiers and politicians could do everything they could, but mothers, fathers, grandmothers, grandfathers, wives, and children under artillery shells, hiding in shelters, **prayed the Rosary**.

"That Rosary gave strength and was around the neck of every Croatian defender," he says. He also emphasizes as equally important the priests who stayed with the people. He calls all of this fateful.

He concludes that the Lord wanted the Croats to remain "on the remnants of the remnants." They did not endure in every part of the area, but Kordić thanks God that they survived in central Bosnia, **"in hope against all hope"**.

sections.subtitle: Obitelj koja nije otišla i pogled na Ahmiće
sections.screenshot_description: Gost započinje odgovor na pitanje što se dogodilo u Ahmićima
sections.content:
Krunoslav napominje da je Venera tijekom rata ostala u Bosni iako je imala priliku otići u Hrvatsku. Zatim postavlja ključno pitanje: **što se zapravo dogodilo u Ahmićima**, zbog kojih je Kordić završio u Haagu?

Kordić najprije potvrđuje da su u ratu ostali supruga, troje djece (Vladimir, Marija i najmlađa Elizabeta), njezini i njegovi roditelji te braća i sestre. Objašnjava da se to podrazumijevalo: ako od drugih traži da izdrže, mora i sam dati primjer, s obitelji koja dijeli „i dobro i zlo“.

O Ahmićima govori kao političar koji je, kaže, pratio i znao što se događa. Izražava tugu zbog žrtava i želi pokoj vječni svim poginulima, „i na našoj i na njihovoj strani“. Ipak, smatra da se ne smiju iznositi neistine, pa navodi svoje argumente:

- selo je, tvrdi, bilo **vojni cilj** s naoružanim ljudima, a u njemu su poginuli i hrvatski branitelji, što po njegovu mišljenju ne bi bilo moguće da je riječ o nebranjenom cilju;
- i suci koje opisuje kao njemu nesklone utvrdili su, prema njegovim riječima, da su neki ciljevi bili legitimni, primjerice ako se s minareta pucalo iz trocijevca;
- prostor je bio strateški: da je tog jutra presječena cesta, Lašvanska bi dolina bila podijeljena i Hrvati u njoj, smatra, ne bi opstali.

Posebno ga žalosti, kaže, uveličavanje brojki. Na njegovu suđenju spominjalo se **76 poginulih**, a njegove i druge procjene govore o šezdesetak. Ne želi ulaziti u to, ali naglašava da je tragedija jednaka i sa 60 i sa 76 poginulih te da s godinama ne treba „ići na 116“. Uspoređuje to s rastom brojki kakav se događao kod Jasenovca. Ističe da time ne želi umanjiti žrtvu nego tražiti poštivanje činjenica i svake žrtve: „Istina će nas sve osloboditi.“

magisterium.assessment: U prikazanom odlomku obiteljska solidarnost i osobno preuzimanje teškoća predstavljeni su kao važni, što može biti spojivo s kršćanskom odgovornošću, ali sam tekst ne omogućuje prosudbu tvrdnji o Ahmićima niti načina na koji su ondje stradali civili. Budući da je odlomak prekinut prije odgovora na pitanje što se dogodilo, njegova je teološka usklađenost samo djelomično procjenjiva.
concerns: Obrazloženje da obitelj ostaje jer govornik mora dati primjer drugima može se razumjeti kao solidarnost, ali bez dodatnog konteksta nije jasno jesu li uzeti u obzir sigurnost i sloboda članova obitelji.
Odlomak postavlja pitanje o Ahmićima, no ne iznosi činjenice o događaju, žrtvama ili odgovornosti; zato se iz njega ne može prosuditi priznaje li patnju civila i poštuje li istinu.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički pogled na rat ne dopušta da se hrabrost ili odanost vlastitoj zajednici odvoje od zaštite ljudskog života i moralnih ograničenja uporabe sile; rat je zlo koje treba nastojati spriječiti, a civili i njihove patnje zahtijevaju posebnu pozornost. Crkva također razlikuje oprost od površnog umanjivanja zla: traženje pravde i nepristrano utvrđivanje odgovornosti nužni su, uz otvorenost pomirenju.

citations.document_author: United States Conference of Catholic Bishops

magisterium.assessment_en: In the presented excerpt, family solidarity and personal acceptance of hardship are presented as important, which can be compatible with Christian responsibility, but the text itself does not allow for a judgment of the claims about Ahmići nor of the manner in which civilians suffered there. Since the excerpt is cut off before the answer to the question of what happened, its theological alignment is only partially assessable.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic view on war does not permit courage or loyalty to one's own community to be separated from the protection of human life and the moral limitations on the use of force; war is an evil that one should strive to prevent, and civilians and their suffering require special attention. The Church also distinguishes forgiveness from a superficial diminishing of evil: seeking justice and impartially establishing responsibility are necessary, along with openness to reconciliation.
concerns_en: The justification that the family remains because the speaker must set an example for others can be understood as solidarity, but without additional context it is not clear whether the safety and freedom of the family members were taken into account.

The excerpt raises a question about Ahmići, but does not present facts about the event, victims, or responsibility; therefore, it cannot be judged from it whether it acknowledges the suffering of civilians and respects the truth.

sections.subtitle_en: The family that did not leave and a view on Ahmići
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest begins the answer to the question of what happened in Ahmići
sections.content_en:
Krunoslav notes that Venera remained in Bosnia during the war even though she had the opportunity to go to Croatia. Then he asks the key question: **what actually happened in Ahmići**, because of which Kordić ended up in The Hague?

Kordić first confirms that during the war his wife, three children (Vladimir, Marija, and the youngest Elizabeta), her and his parents, and brothers and sisters stayed behind. He explains that this was taken for granted: if he asks others to endure, he must set an example himself, with a family that shares „both good and bad“.

He speaks about Ahmići as a politician who, he says, followed and knew what was happening. He expresses sorrow for the victims and wishes eternal rest to all who died, „both on our side and on their side“. Nevertheless, he believes that falsehoods must not be presented, so he cites his arguments:

- the village, he claims, was a **military target** with armed men, and Croatian defenders also died in it, which in his opinion would not have been possible if it were an undefended target;
- even the judges, whom he describes as unfavorable to him, determined, according to his words, that some targets were legitimate, for example if a triple-barrel gun was fired from a minaret;
- the area was strategic: if the road had been cut that morning, the Lašva Valley would have been divided and the Croats in it, he believes, would not have survived.

He says he is particularly saddened by the exaggeration of figures. At his trial, **76 dead** were mentioned, and his and other estimates speak of around sixty. He does not want to go into that, but emphasizes that the tragedy is the same with both 60 and 76 dead and that over the years one should not „go to 116“. He compares this with the growth of figures such as occurred with Jasenovac. He emphasizes that by doing so he does not wish to diminish the sacrifice, but to demand respect for facts and for every victim: „The truth will set us all free.“

sections.subtitle: Pljuvanje na mrežama, argumenti iz presude i jedna domovina u srcu
sections.screenshot_description: Kordić spominje Luku Mišetića i njegove objave na Twitteru o presudi
sections.content:
Kordić kaže da nema Facebook ni druge društvene mreže i da ih ne prati. Ponekad mu supruga pokaže što se piše. Na takve napade, koji idu „od pečenja djeteta do ovoga, onoga“, nikada nije odgovarao.

Kao osobu „najviše verziranu za Ahmiće“ navodi **Luku Mišetića**, odvjetnika **Ante Gotovine**. Prema Kordiću, Mišetić je na Twitteru, na dan najžešćih napada, pozvao odvjetnike iz Sarajeva da s njim rasprave konkretne članke i aline presude u predmetu Kordić: „Nemojte govoriti ono što nema u presudi.“ Nitko se, kaže Kordić, nikada nije imenom i prezimenom odazvao da argumentima, a ne histerijom, suoči stavove.

Navodi i nedavni primjer koji ga je pogodio. Poslali su mu snimku na kojoj šef pravne katedre u **Zenici** pred djecom petog i šestog razreda uspoređuje Hrvatsku, hrvatski narod i hrvatske zastave s **Trećim Reichom**. „Ne ide to tako govoriti, a želimo graditi budućnost zajedničke domovine“, upozorava. Poziva na traženje zajedničkog rješenja kako bi država funkcionirala.

Na kraju iznosi svoje osobno stajalište: domovina je za njega jedna, a to je Hrvatska. Kroz povijest je bila „ovaka i onaka“, danas je u dvije države, ali on u srcu ne dijeli Hrvatsku i Bosnu i Hercegovinu: **„ona je jedna za mene“**.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim načelima jer ne uzvraća na uvrede te zagovara raspravu utemeljenu na točnom čitanju presude, a ne na tvrdnjama koje ona ne sadrži. U njemu se, međutim, ne iznosi izričit teološki nauk niti se iz samog isječka može prosuditi istinitost svih navoda o presudi i događajima.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički pristup javnoj raspravi traži izbjegavanje klevete i vrijeđanja, ali ne isključuje ispravno i obzirno ispravljanje pogrešaka; sveti Franjo Saleški naglašava da se o drugima govori pravedno, bez pretjerivanja i s ljubavlju prema osobi. Papa Franjo upozorava da digitalni prostori lako postaju mjesta klevete i verbalnog nasilja, pa je uzdržavanje od uzvraćanja uvredama moralno značajno.
magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely aligned with Catholic principles because it does not retaliate to insults and advocates a discussion based on an accurate reading of the verdict, rather than on claims that it does not contain. In it, however, no explicit theological teaching is presented, nor can the truth of all statements about the verdict and events be judged from the excerpt itself.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic approach to public debate requires the avoidance of calumny and insults, but does not exclude the correct and considerate correction of errors; Saint Francis de Sales emphasizes that one should speak of others justly, without exaggeration and with love for the person. Pope Francis warns that digital spaces easily become places of defamation and verbal violence, so refraining from retaliating with insults is morally significant.

sections.subtitle_en: Spitting on networks, arguments from the verdict, and one homeland in the heart
sections.screenshot_description_en: Kordić mentions Luka Mišetić and his posts on Twitter about the verdict
sections.content_en:
Kordić says that he does not have Facebook or other social networks and that he does not follow them. Sometimes his wife shows him what is being written. To such attacks, which go "from roasting a child to this, that," he has never responded.

As the person "most versed in Ahmići" he cites **Luka Mišetić**, the lawyer of **Ante Gotovina**. According to Kordić, Mišetić on Twitter, on the day of the fiercest attacks, invited lawyers from Sarajevo to discuss with him specific articles and indentations of the verdict in the Kordić case: "Do not speak what is not in the verdict." No one, Kordić says, has ever responded by full name to confront views with arguments, rather than hysteria.

He also cites a recent example that struck him. They sent him a recording in which the head of the law department in **Zenica** compares Croatia, the Croatian people, and Croatian flags with the **Third Reich** in front of fifth- and sixth-grade children. "It does not work to speak that way, while we want to build the future of a common homeland," he warns. He calls for seeking a common solution so that the state would function.

In the end, he presents his personal stance: the homeland is one for him, and that is Croatia. Throughout history it was "like this and like that," today it is in two states, but in his heart he does not divide Croatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina: **"it is one for me"**.

sections.subtitle: Optužnica, život u ilegali i poruka Tuđmanu i Šušku: „Zovite me, ja ću tog dana ići“
sections.screenshot_description: Gost objašnjava da se nikada nije želio skrivati te da je bio spreman dragovoljno otići u Haag
sections.content:
Krunoslav pita kako je doživio poziv u Haag: je li otišao dragovoljno ili je osjećao averziju i razočaranje. Kordić odgovara da nije bilo ni averzije ni bilo kakvog negativnog raspoloženja.

Optužnica je stigla oko **Daytonskog sporazuma**, rješenja koje Kordić naziva nepravednim: zaustavilo je rat, ali nije donijelo rješenje. S optužnicom je živio godinu i pol. Dio tog vremena kretao se slobodno, a dio proveo u nekoj vrsti ilegale, ne znajući ni od koga se skriva ni gdje.

Ipak, naglašava da se nikada nije želio skrivati. Vrhovništvu Hrvatske, predsjedniku **Tuđmanu** i ministru **Šušku**, poručio je: „Kada bude najbolje za Hrvatsku, ja sam tu. Zovite me, ja ću tog dana ići.“ Tako je i bilo. Kad je osjetio da je došao trenutak, otišao je jer se, kaže, nije imao zbog čega skrivati i htio je čuti što imaju protiv njega i njegove „braće“. Tada je u Haag otišlo desetak Hrvata.

magisterium.assessment: Prikazani dio uglavnom je činjenično-politički iskaz o optužnici i osobnom doživljaju, a ne izlaganje teološkog nauka; u njemu nema očitog proturječja katoličkom nauku ili Svetom pismu. Tvrdnja da je Daytonski sporazum bio nepravedan jest politička procjena i iz ovog odlomka nije moguće prosuditi njezinu činjeničnu osnovu ni moralnu opravdanost.
concerns: Ocjena Daytonskog sporazuma kao nepravednog izrečena je bez obrazloženja, pa se ne može procijeniti odnosi li se na konkretne posljedice za pravdu i zajedničko dobro ili samo izražava političko nezadovoljstvo.
Odlomak je prekinut nakon riječi „Ipak, naglašava da…”, pa se ne može procijeniti nastavak, osobito eventualne tvrdnje o odgovornosti, suđenju ili odnosu prema žrtvama.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički nauk drži da želja za mirom ne isključuje odgovornost za zločine: svjetovna pravda može i treba kažnjavati zločine, ali ne smije postati slijepa osveta, nego treba služiti općem dobru i pridobivanju onih koji su pogriješili. U kontekstu balkanskih ratova Ivan Pavao II. također je isticao da se zahtjev za pravdom mora držati zajedno s Kristovim pozivom na oproštenje, bez površnog umanjivanja zla.

citations.document_title: To the President of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina (September 8, 1994) - Speech

magisterium.assessment_en: The presented part is mainly a factual-political statement about the indictment and personal experience, not an exposition of theological teaching; in it there is no obvious contradiction to Catholic teaching or Sacred Scripture. The claim that the Dayton Agreement was unjust is a political assessment, and from this excerpt it is not possible to judge its factual basis nor its moral justification.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic teaching holds that the desire for peace does not exclude responsibility for crimes: secular justice can and should punish crimes, but it must not become blind revenge; rather, it should serve the common good and the winning over of those who have erred. In the context of the Balkan wars, John Paul II also emphasized that the demand for justice must be held together with Christ's call to forgiveness, without superficial minimization of evil.
concerns_en: The assessment of the Dayton Agreement as unjust was stated without explanation, so it cannot be evaluated whether it refers to concrete consequences for justice and the common good or merely expresses political dissatisfaction.

The excerpt is interrupted after the words „Nevertheless, he emphasizes that…”, so the continuation cannot be evaluated, especially possible claims about responsibility, the trial, or the attitude toward the victims.

sections.subtitle_en: The indictment, life underground and a message to Tuđman and Šušak: „Call me, I will go on that day“
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest explains that he never wanted to hide and that he was ready to go voluntarily to The Hague
sections.content_en:
Krunoslav asks how he experienced the summons to The Hague: whether he went voluntarily or felt aversion and disappointment. Kordić answers that there was neither aversion nor any kind of negative mood.

The indictment arrived around the **Dayton Agreement**, a solution that Kordić calls unjust: it stopped the war, but did not bring a solution. He lived with the indictment for a year and a half. Part of that time he moved freely, and part he spent in a kind of underground, not knowing from whom he was hiding nor where.

Nevertheless, he emphasizes that he never wanted to hide. To the leadership of Croatia, President **Tuđman** and Minister **Šušak**, he sent the message: „When it is best for Croatia, I am here. Call me, I will go on that day.“ And so it was. When he felt that the moment had arrived, he went because, he says, he had nothing to hide from and wanted to hear what they had against him and his „brothers“. At that time, about ten Croats went to The Hague.

sections.subtitle: 6. listopada 1997.: na ribičkom stolcu NATO-ova aviona, s krunicom u ruci
sections.screenshot_description: Kordić se prisjeća leta iz Splita za Nizozemsku
sections.content:
Kordić se jasno sjeća datuma: **6. listopada 1997.**, sunčan dan u splitskoj zračnoj luci. Ondje je dao kratku izjavu koju je na engleski prevodio prevoditelj iz Ureda predsjednika Tuđmana. Prisutan je bio i američki visoki predstavnik **Gelbard**.

Nakon ispraćaja ukrcali su se u stari NATO-ov zrakoplov bez pravih sjedala, umjesto kojih su bili ribički stolci. Kordić je sjeo, s krunicom u ruci, i tijekom leta do Nizozemske utonuo u san.

Prvi dan u Haagu uzeli su mu otiske prstiju i fotografirali ga, a zatim je ušao u sobu u kojoj će ostati ne znajući koliko dugo. Od prvog dana uzeo je krunicu. Kaže da Gospodinu nikada nije postavio pitanje koliko će to trajati. Molio je samo: **„Gospodine, nemoj mi otvoriti vrata dok ne bude tvoja volja.“** Dodaje da bi prihvatio i Božju volju da nikada ne izađe.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim naukom: krunica se spominje kao pobožni predmet, a ne kao zamjena za Boga ili kao sredstvo koje samo po sebi jamči ishod. Budući da je riječ pretežno o povijesnom pripovijedanju, tekst ne iznosi snažnu teološku tvrdnju koju bi trebalo prosuđivati.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolička tradicija krunicu prepoznaje kao oblik molitve i pobožnosti povezane s Marijinim zagovorom; samo držanje krunice ipak ne otkriva što je osoba u tom trenutku molila niti kakvo je značenje pridavala putovanju. Ako se događaj tumači u svjetlu Božje providnosti, treba razlikovati Božje dopuštanje nekog događaja od moralnog odobravanja svih ljudskih postupaka povezanih s njim.

citations.document_title: Address Vous avez voulu to participants in the 10th International Congress of Historical Sciences (September 7, 1955)

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely aligned with Catholic teaching: the Rosary is mentioned as a devotional object, not as a substitute for God or as a means that in itself guarantees an outcome. Since it is predominantly a historical narrative, the text does not make a strong theological claim that would need to be judged.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic tradition recognizes the Rosary as a form of prayer and devotion connected with Mary's intercession; merely holding the Rosary, however, does not reveal what the person was praying at that moment nor what meaning they attached to the journey. If the event is interpreted in the light of God's providence, one must distinguish God's permission of an event from the moral approval of all human actions connected with it.

sections.subtitle_en: October 6, 1997: on a fisherman's stool in a NATO plane, with a Rosary in hand
sections.screenshot_description_en: Kordić recalls the flight from Split to the Netherlands
sections.content_en:
Kordić clearly remembers the date: **October 6, 1997**, a sunny day at the Split airport. There he gave a short statement that was translated into English by an interpreter from the Office of President Tuđman. The American high representative **Gelbard** was also present.

After the send-off, they boarded an old NATO plane without real seats, in place of which were fishing stools. Kordić sat down, with a Rosary in hand, and during the flight to the Netherlands fell into sleep.

The first day in The Hague they took his fingerprints and photographed him, and then he entered a room in which he would stay without knowing for how long. From the first day he took up the Rosary. He says that he never asked the Lord the question of how long it would last. He only prayed: **“Lord, do not open the door for me until it is your will.”** He adds that he would also have accepted God's will to never get out.

sections.subtitle: Osamnaest mjeseci duhovne obnove u ćeliji dva sa četiri metra
sections.screenshot_description: Gost opisuje ćeliju sa željeznim krevetom i improviziranim oltarićem
sections.content:
Krunoslav pita je li optužnicu doživio kao izdaju svega što je učinio za hrvatski narod u Bosni. Kordić se najprije obraća voditelju imenom i napominje da su na „ti“ jer se poznaju iz javne molitve krunice na trgovima. Zatim objašnjava da je bio tužan, ali ne samo zbog sebe, nego i zbog mnogih iz vojnog i političkog vodstva Hrvata u Lašvanskoj dolini koji su optuženi, „znajući što je stvarno bilo“. Prema njegovim riječima, Hrvati su bili napadnuti, a neutralni promatrači procijenili su odnos snaga na **7 do 10 prema 1** u korist onih koji su ih držali u okruženju.

Ipak, kaže, Bog čovjeka stvori „borcem“. Uzeo je krunicu i molio. Do prvog izlaska u sudnicu prošlo je **18 mjeseci** u pripremama, uz povremene posjete odvjetnika. Kordić ih je iskoristio, kako kaže, „u najboljem smislu“: kao životnu duhovnu obnovu kakvu nikada nije prošao „ni prije ni poslije“ i koju je osobno vodio Gospodin. „Dao mi je ruku i po toj sobici sam ja s njime tisuće puta prošao“, opisuje. Gospodin ga je, kaže, čistio od grijeha, egoizma i „svih natruha“.

Ćelija je bila dva sa četiri metra, sa željeznim krevetom, stolićem i improviziranim oltarićem sa svetim slikama. Iz nje je izlazio samo u šetnju i u dnevni boravak. To razdoblje uspoređuje s majkom koja nedonošče hrani majčinim mlijekom: Gospodin mu je tada davao „nektar“ za sve što će uslijediti.

magisterium.assessment: Izraz tuge zbog optuženih i tvrdnja da su Hrvati bili napadnuti sami po sebi nisu protivni katoličkom nauku, ali ovaj izvadak prikazuje sukob ponajprije iz perspektive jedne nacionalne skupine i ne daje dovoljno konteksta za procjenu povijesnih tvrdnji. Katolički pristup zahtijeva objektivno utvrđivanje istine i pravedno suđenje odgovornima, bez kolektivnog okrivljavanja ili unaprijed pretpostavljene nevinosti.
concerns: Formulacija da se govori „znajući što je stvarno bilo” može zvučati kao zaključak da optuženi nisu odgovorni, premda izvadak ne kaže izričito da su nevini; odgovornost se mora utvrđivati pojedinačno i nepristrano.
Prikaz da su Hrvati bili napadnuti ostaje jednostran bez šireg konteksta o žrtvama i djelima svih strana; nije moguće iz ovog odlomka potvrditi ni osporiti njegovu povijesnu točnost.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkva istodobno priznaje potrebu da krivci budu privedeni pravdi i poziva na oprost, koji ne znači površno umanjivanje zla niti odustajanje od nepristranosti. Ivan Pavao II. posebno je upozorio da se o tragedijama na Balkanu mora prosuđivati objektivno te da agresiju i njezino opravdavanje treba osuditi, dok se legitimna obrana može dopustiti.
magisterium.assessment_en: The expression of sadness for the accused and the claim that the Croats were attacked are not in themselves contrary to Catholic teaching, but this excerpt presents the conflict primarily from the perspective of one national group and does not provide enough context to assess the historical claims. The Catholic approach requires the objective establishment of the truth and a fair trial for those responsible, without collective blame or presumed innocence in advance.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Church simultaneously recognizes the need for the guilty to be brought to justice and calls for forgiveness, which does not mean superficially downplaying evil nor abandoning impartiality. John Paul II specifically warned that the tragedies in the Balkans must be judged objectively and that aggression and its justification should be condemned, while legitimate defense may be permitted.
concerns_en: The formulation that one speaks „knowing what really happened” may sound like a conclusion that the accused are not responsible, although the excerpt does not explicitly state that they are innocent; responsibility must be determined individually and impartially.

The portrayal that the Croats were attacked remains one-sided without a broader context about the victims and actions of all sides; it is not possible from this passage either to confirm or refute its historical accuracy.

sections.subtitle_en: Eighteen months of spiritual renewal in a two by four meter cell
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest describes the cell with an iron bed and an improvised little altar
sections.content_en:
Krunoslav asks whether he experienced the indictment as a betrayal of everything he had done for the Croatian people in Bosnia. Kordić first addresses the host by name and notes that they are on informal terms because they know each other from public prayer of the Rosary on squares. He then explains that he was sad, but not only because of himself, but also because of many from the military and political leadership of the Croats in Lašvanska dolina who were indicted, „knowing what really happened“. According to his words, the Croats were attacked, and neutral observers estimated the balance of power at **7 to 10 to 1** in favor of those who held them encircled.

Nevertheless, he says, God created man as a „fighter“. He took the Rosary and prayed. Until the first appearance in the courtroom, **18 months** passed in preparations, with occasional visits from lawyers. Kordić used them, as he says, „in the best sense“: as a life's spiritual renewal such as he had never undergone „neither before nor after“ and which was personally led by the Lord. „He gave me his hand and through that little room I walked with him thousands of times,“ he describes. The Lord, he says, cleansed him of sin, egoism, and „all taints“.

The cell was two by four meters, with an iron bed, a small table, and an improvised little altar with holy images. He only left it for a walk and to the common room. He compares that period to a mother feeding a premature baby with mother's milk: the Lord was giving him „nectar“ then for everything that was to follow.

sections.subtitle: Tri sata ujutro, uoči prvog ročišta: „Tvoju parnicu ću ja voditi“
sections.screenshot_description: Kordić opisuje svjetlo koje ga je probudilo u tri sata ujutro i prvi susret sa živim Bogom
sections.content:
Nakon 18 mjeseci došao je **12. travnja 1999.**, dan kad je s optuženikom iz istog predmeta, „subratom“ Marijom Čerkezom, prvi put trebao izaći u sudnicu. Večer prije legao je, kako kaže, s „radosnim nestrpljenjem“, pomolio se i zaspao.

„U tri sata budi me svjetlo koje nije od ovoga svijeta. To je moj prvi susret sa živim Bogom“, svjedoči. Na Krunoslavljevo pitanje je li to bio san, odgovara da je bio budan i da je jednostavno znao da je Gospodin ondje. Svjetlo je obasjalo mračnu prostoriju, a doživljaj uspoređuje s onim što je doživjela sveta **Faustina Kowalska** sa zrakama.

Kaže da je od radosti „useptao“, ne znajući što reći, a u srcu je čuo glas: **„Dragi moj sine, dragi moj prijatelju, ne boj se, s tobom sam uvijek i u svemu, tvoju parnicu ću ja voditi.“**

Od tog dana, objašnjava, u ljudskom je smislu činio sve što je mogao. Opisuje raspored u sudnici: odvjetnici malo dalje od njega, svjedok još dalje, suci uzdignuti s lijeve strane, a tužitelj na drugoj strani. Pitanja koja bi se sjetio pisao je na papiriće koje je stražar nosio obrani. Ipak, znao je da će biti onako kako je Božja volja. Tog jutra nazvao je suprugu i rekao joj da se osjeća kao leptirić koji lebdi: „Oni neka rade što žele, a meni je kao da na svadbu idem.“ Ta „svadba“, dodaje, traje do danas.

magisterium.assessment: Opis mogućeg osobnog mističnog iskustva nije sam po sebi protivan katoličkom nauku: Crkva priznaje mogućnost susreta s Bogom i privatnih objava, ali svjedočanstvo pojedinca ne postaje time obvezujuće za vjernike. Tvrdnju da je govorio Gospodin treba prihvatiti razborito i razlučivati prema njezinoj usmjerenosti Kristu i plodovima, a ne kao potvrđenu nadnaravnu činjenicu.
concerns: Iz odlomka se ne može utvrditi je li doživljaj bio nadnaravan, san ili drugo osobno iskustvo; sama sigurnost govornika nije dovoljna da Crkva potvrdi objavu.
Naslovna tvrdnja „Tvoju parnicu ću ja voditi” ne smije se shvatiti kao jamstvo određenog sudskog ishoda ili previše izravno tumačiti Božju volju bez daljnjeg razlučivanja.
magisterium.enrichment: Sveto pismo poznaje viđenja i posebna iskustva Božje prisutnosti, pa izvještaj o takvom iskustvu nije nevjerojatan samo zato što je neobičan. Ipak, privatna objava ne dopunjuje niti nadmašuje konačnu objavu u Kristu; njezina se vjerodostojnost prosuđuje prema tome vodi li Kristu i hrani li vjeru, nadu i ljubav. Vjernici nisu obvezni prihvatiti privatno svjedočanstvo, ali ga mogu razmotriti razborito i u skladu s crkvenim naukom.
magisterium.assessment_en: The description of a possible personal mystical experience is not in itself contrary to Catholic teaching: the Church recognizes the possibility of encounters with God and private revelations, but an individual's testimony does not thereby become binding on the faithful. The claim that the Lord spoke should be accepted prudently and discerned according to its orientation toward Christ and its fruits, and not as a confirmed supernatural fact.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Sacred Scripture knows visions and special experiences of God's presence, so an account of such an experience is not incredible merely because it is unusual. Nevertheless, private revelation does not complete or surpass the definitive revelation in Christ; its credibility is judged by whether it leads to Christ and nourishes faith, hope, and love. The faithful are not obligated to accept private testimony, but they may consider it prudently and in accordance with Church teaching.
concerns_en: From the passage, it cannot be determined whether the experience was supernatural, a dream, or another personal experience; the speaker's certainty alone is not sufficient for the Church to confirm a revelation.
The title claim "I will lead your lawsuit" must not be understood as a guarantee of a specific judicial outcome or interpret God's will too directly without further discernment.

sections.subtitle_en: Three o'clock in the morning, on the eve of the first court hearing: "I will lead your lawsuit"
sections.screenshot_description_en: Kordić describes the light that woke him up at three o'clock in the morning and his first encounter with the living God
sections.content_en:
After 18 months came **April 12, 1999**, the day when, together with the defendant from the same case, "confrere" Marijo Čerkez, he was to appear in the courtroom for the first time. The evening before, he went to bed, as he says, with "joyful impatience," prayed, and fell asleep.

"At three o'clock, a light that is not of this world wakes me. That is my first encounter with the living God," he testifies. To Krunoslav's question whether that was a dream, he replies that he was awake and that he simply knew that the Lord was there. The light illuminated the dark room, and he compares the experience to what Saint **Faustina Kowalska** experienced with the rays.

He says that from joy he "gasped," not knowing what to say, and in his heart he heard a voice: **"My dear son, my dear friend, do not be afraid, I am with you always and in everything, I will lead your lawsuit."**

From that day on, he explains, in the human sense he did everything he could. He describes the layout in the courtroom: the lawyers a little further from him, the witness even further, the judges elevated on the left side, and the prosecutor on the other side. The questions he would think of he wrote on slips of paper that the guard carried to the defense. Still, he knew that it would be as God's will is. That morning he called his wife and told her that he felt like a little butterfly hovering: "Let them do whatever they want, but to me it is as if I were going to a wedding." That "wedding," he adds, lasts to this day.

sections.subtitle: Papa Ivan Pavao II. „visok kao Biokovo“ i klica duhovnog poziva
sections.screenshot_description: Gost opisuje viđenje pape Ivana Pavla II. iznad Veprica
sections.content:
Krunoslav primjećuje da je to bilo mistično iskustvo, uz ogradu da ne zna je li izraz teološki točan. Kordić potvrđuje da je takvih susreta bilo još dva ili tri, ali o većini ne želi govoriti.

Izdvaja posljednji, iz **2003. godine**, uoči proglašenja blaženim **Ivana Merza** u Banjoj Luci. Probudio se i ugledao svetog oca **papu Ivana Pavla II.**, „visokog kao Biokovo“, iznad **Veprica**. Taj kraj dobro poznaje jer je ondje često ljetovao još kao dijete. Papa mu je pružio ruku i dva-tri puta ga pozvao, a Kordić se pred njim osjećao „kao mali miš“. Uzvratio mu je ruku.

U tom iskustvu danas vidi klicu duhovnog poziva koji tada nije prepoznao. Postupno ga je razaznavao tek deset-petnaest godina kasnije, u razgovorima sa svećenicima. Od tada je, kaže, njegov hod za Kristom postao intenzivniji.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim naukom jer osobno iskustvo prikazuje kao subjektivno i neizvjesno, a ne kao obveznu istinu vjere ili nadopunu Evanđelja. Tvrdnja o viđenju ostaje privatno svjedočanstvo koje se ne može potvrditi samo na temelju ovog ulomka.
concerns: Nije navedeno je li iskustvo crkveno razlučeno; zato ga ne treba predstavljati kao potvrđenu nadnaravnu objavu niti kao dokaz katoličkog nauka.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički nauk uči da privatne objave, čak i kada su crkveno priznate, ne pripadaju pologu vjere i ne mogu dopuniti Kristovu konačnu Objavu; mogu samo pomoći vjernicima da je potpunije žive, pa prihvaćanje pojedinog svjedočanstva nije obvezno. Ivan Merz proglašen je blaženim u Banjoj Luci 22. lipnja 2003., što je u skladu s vremenskim okvirom koji odlomak navodi.

citations.document_author: Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely aligned with Catholic teaching because it portrays a personal experience as subjective and uncertain, rather than as a binding truth of faith or a supplement to the Gospel. The claim of a vision remains a private testimony that cannot be confirmed on the basis of this excerpt alone.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic teaching teaches that private revelations, even when ecclesiastically approved, do not belong to the deposit of faith and cannot supplement Christ's definitive Revelation; they can only help the faithful to live it more fully, so the acceptance of an individual testimony is not obligatory. Ivan Merz was beatified in Banja Luka on June 22, 2003, which is consistent with the timeframe mentioned in the passage.
concerns_en: It is not stated whether the experience has been ecclesiastically discerned; therefore, it should not be presented as a confirmed supernatural revelation or as proof of Catholic teaching.

sections.subtitle_en: Pope John Paul II "as tall as Biokovo" and the seed of a spiritual vocation
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest describes a vision of Pope John Paul II above Vepric
sections.content_en:
Krunoslav notes that it was a mystical experience, with the caveat that he does not know whether the term is theologically accurate. Kordić confirms that there were two or three more such encounters, but he does not want to speak about most of them.

He singles out the last one, from the **year 2003**, on the eve of the beatification of **Ivan Merz** in Banja Luka. He woke up and saw the Holy Father **Pope John Paul II**, "as tall as Biokovo", above **Vepric**. He knows that region well because he often spent his summers there as a child. The Pope extended his hand to him and called him two or three times, and Kordić felt before him "like a little mouse". He returned his hand.

In that experience today he sees the seed of a spiritual vocation that he did not recognize at the time. He gradually discerned it only ten to fifteen years later, in conversations with priests. Since then, he says, his walk after Christ became more intense.

sections.subtitle: Scheveningen: bodljikava žica, „podmornica“ i dvadeset mjeseci suđenja
sections.screenshot_description: Kordić opisuje pritvorsku jedinicu u Scheveningenu i zgradu zvanu podmornica
sections.content:
Pritvorska jedinica nalazila se u **Scheveningenu**, malom primorskom mjestu koje Kordić opisuje kao mondeno turističko odredište. Galebovi su doletjeli dok su bili u šetnji, „ali mi smo bodljikavom žicom bili ograđeni“.

Prve četiri godine proveo je u zgradi koju su zatvorenici zvali **„podmornica“**. Ondje se nije mogao otvoriti nijedan prozor, a zrak se ubacivao umjetno kroz instalacije koje se nisu čistile. Bio je to, kaže, „život pod staklenim zvonom“. Zgrada je imala 32 sobe. Kad je optuženika bilo sve više, premješteni su u objekt nazvan **„96“** prema broju soba, gdje se prozor barem mogao malo odškrinuti. U svakoj sobi bio je po jedan zatvorenik.

Suđenje je trajalo **20 mjeseci**, svakoga dana od ponedjeljka do petka, „od jutra do mraka“. U Haag su ga vozili u lisicama i uz posebne mjere, a pri dolasku i povratku slijedili su pregledi i skidanje. Kordić zaključuje kratko: „Procedure su se obavljale, proces je trajao.“

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je pretežno opisno svjedočanstvo o zatvorskim uvjetima i ne iznosi tvrdnje koje bi bile u sukobu s katoličkim naukom ili Svetim pismom. Katolički nauk podupire zabrinutost zbog mogućeg nečovječnog postupanja, ali sam odlomak ne omogućuje provjeru točnosti opisanih uvjeta.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolička Crkva naučava da zatvorenici, neovisno o mogućoj krivnji, zadržavaju ljudsko dostojanstvo i imaju pravo na postupanje koje ga poštuje; kazna treba služiti i obnovi pravde i rehabilitaciji, a ne ponižavanju osobe. Zato su tvrdnje o nečistom zraku i nemogućnosti otvaranja prozora teološki važne kao opis mogućih uvjeta koji traže ozbiljnu pozornost, premda njihovu činjeničnu točnost treba procjenjivati neovisno. Kristovo poistovjećivanje s onima koji su u zatvoru poziva kršćane na suosjećanje i poštovanje prema zatvorenicima, neovisno o tome što je sudski postupak utvrdio.

citations.document_title: Pastoral Visit to Rebibbia Prison - Rome (December 18, 2011)
To chaplains of Italian prisons (November 24, 1983) - Speech
To the prisoners in the regional jail of Płock (June 7, 1991) - Speech

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is predominantly a descriptive testimony about prison conditions and does not present claims that would be in conflict with Catholic teaching or Sacred Scripture. Catholic teaching supports concern over possible inhumane treatment, but the passage itself does not enable verification of the accuracy of the described conditions.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic Church teaches that prisoners, regardless of possible guilt, retain human dignity and have the right to treatment that respects it; punishment should serve both the restoration of justice and rehabilitation, and not the humiliation of the person. Therefore, claims of unclean air and the impossibility of opening windows are theologically important as a description of possible conditions that demand serious attention, although their factual accuracy should be evaluated independently. Christ's identification with those who are in prison calls Christians to compassion and respect toward prisoners, regardless of what the judicial process has established.

sections.subtitle_en: Scheveningen: barbed wire, "submarine" and twenty months of trial
sections.screenshot_description_en: Kordić describes the detention unit in Scheveningen and the building called the submarine
sections.content_en:
The detention unit was located in **Scheveningen**, a small seaside town that Kordić describes as a fashionable tourist destination. Seagulls flew in while they were taking a walk, "but we were enclosed by barbed wire."

He spent the first four years in a building the prisoners called the **"submarine"**. Not a single window could be opened there, and air was introduced artificially through installations that were not cleaned. It was, he says, "life under a bell jar." The building had 32 rooms. When there were more and more accused persons, they were moved to a facility named **"96"** after the number of rooms, where the window could at least be cracked open a little. There was one prisoner in each room.

The trial lasted **20 months**, every day from Monday to Friday, "from morning to dark." They drove him to The Hague in handcuffs and under special measures, and upon arrival and return, inspections and strip searches followed. Kordić concludes briefly: "Procedures were carried out, the process went on."

sections.subtitle: Gospine poruke iz „plave knjige“ i presuda od 25 godina
sections.screenshot_description: Gost se prisjeća izricanja prvostupanjske presude u veljači 2001.
sections.content:
Kordić se usput prisjeća da je tih dana, uz Bibliju, čitao Gospine poruke oca **Gobbija**, takozvanu **„plavu knjigu“**. U najtežim danima uvijek bi naišao na neku lijepu Gospinu poruku koja bi ga „osokolila“. Ističe da je bio pun Duha Svetoga i radostan unatoč svemu te da tuge nije bilo ni u trenucima presude.

Prvostupanjska presuda izrečena je krajem **veljače 2001.**: **25 godina zatvora**. Supruga i odvjetnici bili su optimistični, a Kordić je za tu prigodu obukao hrvatsko odijelo, narodnu nošnju koju je dobio iz Trogira. Ipak, kaže, u srcu je osjećao da ishod neće biti onakav kakvom su se nadali.

Presudnim smatra iznenađenje iz posljednjih sedam dana postupka. Pojavio se svjedok kojeg su, prema Kordiću, pripremali 30 dana i koji je bio smješten na katu iznad njega, a da obrana to nije znala. Svjedok je trebao potvrditi da je Kordić one noći bio na sastanku na kojem se razgovaralo o Ahmićima. Kordić naglašava da to za njega ne bi bio zločin ni da je bio ondje, ali tvrdi da sedam dana prije ni sedam dana poslije uopće nije išao u taj grad. Svjedok je, kaže, rekao samo da je „čuo“ da je on bio ondje.

Obrana je dovela sve ljude koje je svjedok naveo kao navodne sudionike sastanka. Nizozemski vještaci pregledali su bilježnicu u koju je vojna policija upisivala tko dolazi kod zapovjednika zbornog područja. Kordićeva imena u njoj nije bilo. Vještaci su potvrdili da je bilježnica originalna, da listovi nisu iskidani te su vještačili čak i olovku. Ipak, sud te argumente nije prihvatio.

Kao ilustraciju koliko je optužba, po njegovu mišljenju, stajala „na labavim nogama“, Kordić navodi tužiteljevu rečenicu „Vjerujte nam na riječ“ i slikovitu usporedbu. Kao da mačku ulove kako pije mlijeko ponedjeljkom i srijedom, pa tvrde da je to sigurno činila i ostalim danima, iako to ne mogu dokazati. Presuda je, zaključuje, donesena „na temelju indicija i priča“.

magisterium.assessment: Čitanje duhovnih tekstova i doživljaj radosti usred teške kušnje mogu biti u skladu s kršćanskom nadom: kršćanska radost ne isključuje patnju, nego može postojati zajedno s njom. Ipak, opis „Gospinih poruka” iz knjige o. Gobbija valja razumjeti kao privatnu pobožnost, a ne kao objavu ravnopravnu Svetom pismu ili obvezujući nauk Crkve.
concerns: Odlomak ne navodi da su poruke iz „plave knjige” privatne naravi niti izričito spominje potrebu njihova razlučivanja; zato se ne može zaključiti da ih predstavlja kao službeno potvrđene ili obvezujuće.
magisterium.enrichment: Privatne objave ne nadopunjuju niti zamjenjuju konačnu Božju objavu u Kristu: njihova se vrijednost prosuđuje prema tome vode li dublje Kristu i podupiru li vjeru, nadu i ljubav; svaku proročku tvrdnju treba provjeravati i zadržati ono što je dobro. Kršćanska radost može biti prisutna i u žalosti, jer se oslanja na zajedništvo s Bogom i nadu uskrsnuća, a ne na odsutnost boli.

citations.document_author: Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith

citations.document_title: 11 February 1985: Mass for the sick on the Solemnity of the Blessed Virgin Mary of Lourdes - Homily

magisterium.assessment_en: Reading spiritual texts and experiencing joy in the midst of a difficult trial can be in accordance with Christian hope: Christian joy does not exclude suffering, but can exist alongside it. Nevertheless, the description of "Our Lady's messages" from Fr. Gobbi's book should be understood as private devotion, and not as revelation equal to Sacred Scripture or the binding teaching of the Church.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Private revelations do not complement or replace God's definitive revelation in Christ: their value is judged by whether they lead more deeply to Christ and support faith, hope, and love; every prophetic claim must be tested and what is good retained. Christian joy can be present even in sorrow, because it relies on communion with God and the hope of the resurrection, and not on the absence of pain.
concerns_en: The passage does not state that the messages from the "blue book" are of a private nature, nor does it explicitly mention the need for their discernment; therefore, it cannot be concluded that it presents them as officially confirmed or binding.

sections.subtitle_en: Our Lady's messages from the "blue book" and the 25-year sentence
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest recalls the pronouncement of the first-instance verdict in February 2001.
sections.content_en:
Kordić mentions in passing that in those days, alongside the Bible, he was reading Our Lady's messages of Father **Gobbi**, the so-called **"blue book"**. In the most difficult days, he would always come across some beautiful message from Our Lady that would "encourage" him. He emphasizes that he was full of the Holy Spirit and joyful despite everything, and that there was no sadness even in the moments of the verdict.

The first-instance verdict was pronounced at the end of **February 2001**: **25 years in prison**. His wife and lawyers were optimistic, and Kordić wore a Croatian suit for that occasion, a folk costume that he had received from Trogir. Nevertheless, he says, in his heart he felt that the outcome would not be what they had hoped for.

He considers the surprise from the last seven days of the proceedings to have been decisive. A witness appeared whom, according to Kordić, they had prepared for 30 days and who was housed on the floor above him without the defense knowing it. The witness was supposed to confirm that Kordić was at a meeting that night where Ahmići was discussed. Kordić emphasizes that for him this would not have been a crime even if he had been there, but claims that seven days before or seven days after he did not go to that town at all. The witness, he says, only said that he had "heard" that he was there.

The defense brought all the people whom the witness named as alleged participants in the meeting. Dutch expert witnesses examined the notebook in which the military police recorded who came to see the commander of the operative zone. Kordić's name was not in it. The experts confirmed that the notebook was original, that the pages were not torn out, and they even examined the pencil. Nevertheless, the court did not accept those arguments.

As an illustration of how much the prosecution, in his opinion, stood "on shaky legs", Kordić cites the prosecutor's sentence "Take our word for it" and a vivid comparison. As if a cat were caught drinking milk on Mondays and Wednesdays, and then they claim that it certainly did so on other days as well, even though they cannot prove it. The verdict, he concludes, was made "on the basis of circumstantial evidence and stories".

sections.subtitle: Promjena vlasti u Hrvatskoj i američki odvjetnici koji su branili bez plaće
sections.screenshot_description: Kordić govori o uskraćivanju financiranja obrane nakon promjene vlasti
sections.content:
Uslijedio je **žalbeni postupak**, u kojem je obrana mogla iznijeti dodatne dokaze. Kordić se pritom našao u, kako kaže, specifičnim okolnostima. U Hrvatskoj je došlo do promjene vlasti, a na predsjednika Tuđmana i ministra Šuška „žestoko se obrušavalo“. Njegovoj obrani uskraćena su prava dogovorena još za njihova mandata, pa nova vlast odvjetnike više nije željela plaćati.

Kordić je tada odvjetnicima rekao da ga više ne moraju braniti jer im to nitko neće platiti. No odvjetnici iz Amerike ostali su s njim i vodili postupak još tri godine, u nadi da će neka buduća vlast podmiriti troškove. Obeštećeni nisu bili nikada, a neki od njih danas više nisu živi. „Kad ljudi stranci vam urade tri-četiri godine besplatno obranu…“, kaže s vidljivom zahvalnošću.

To razdoblje opisuje kao posebnu ostavljenost i križ koji je, kako kaže, doživio od „svojih“, uz napomenu da riječ stavlja „pod navodne znakove“. Tvrdi i da su tada falsificirani neki dokumenti te da su u tome sudjelovali i pojedini ministri tadašnje hrvatske vlade. Imena ne želi spominjati, ali dodaje da je to bilo poznato javnosti.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak iznosi opis žalbenog postupka i postupanja odvjetnika, bez tvrdnji koje bi proturječile katoličkom nauku ili Svetom pismu. U skladu s katoličkim naukom je naglasak na poštovanju prava na obranu i dostojanstva zatvorenika, ali sam odlomak ne utvrđuje ni ne sugerira da obrana znači nevinost ili oslobađanje od odgovornosti.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko razumijevanje pravde obuhvaća i zaštitu društva i poštovanje dostojanstva osobe koja je zatvorena; pravedan postupak i mogućnost obrane važni su neovisno o tome kakav će biti ishod suđenja. Odlomak opisuje osobno iskustvo i navodne okolnosti financiranja obrane, koje se ne mogu potvrditi samo teološkom procjenom.

The Parties in the Case. Brief Notes on Chapters 1476-1490, CIC, 1995, Issue 3, pp. 489–514

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage presents a description of the appeals process and the lawyers' actions, without claims that would contradict Catholic teaching or Sacred Scripture. In accordance with Catholic teaching is the emphasis on respect for the right to defense and the dignity of the prisoner, but the passage itself neither establishes nor suggests that a defense means innocence or release from responsibility.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic understanding of justice encompasses both the protection of society and respect for the dignity of the person who is imprisoned; a fair trial and the possibility of defense are important regardless of what the outcome of the trial will be. The passage describes personal experience and alleged circumstances of defense financing, which cannot be confirmed by theological assessment alone.

sections.subtitle_en: Change of government in Croatia and American lawyers who defended without pay
sections.screenshot_description_en: Kordić speaks about the denial of defense funding after the change of government
sections.content_en:
An **appeals process** followed, in which the defense could present additional evidence. Kordić found himself in, as he says, specific circumstances. A change of government took place in Croatia, and President Tuđman and Minister Šušak were being „fiercely attacked“. His defense was denied the rights agreed upon during their mandate, so the new government no longer wanted to pay the lawyers.

Kordić then told the lawyers that they no longer had to defend him because no one would pay them for it. But the lawyers from America stayed with him and led the proceedings for another three years, in the hope that some future government would settle the costs. They were never compensated, and some of them are no longer alive today. „When foreign people do a defense for you for three to four years for free…“, he says with visible gratitude.

He describes that period as a particular abandonment and a cross that he, as he says, experienced from „his own“, noting that he puts the word „in quotation marks“. He also claims that certain documents were falsified at that time and that individual ministers of the then-Croatian government participated in this. He does not want to mention names, but adds that this was known to the public.

sections.subtitle: „Gospe, nemoj da mi mrvice sa stola daju“: žalbena presuda bez umanjenja
sections.screenshot_description: Gost opisuje svoj vapaj međugorskoj Gospi pred čitanje žalbene presude
sections.content:
Ulazeći u sudnicu na izricanje konačne presude, Kordić je, kako kaže, jedini put zavapio **međugorskoj Majci**: „Gospe, usliši me, ali nek bude opet Božja volja. Nemoj da mi mrvice sa stola daju.“ Osjećao je da je obrana podnijela toliko dokaza da mu kazna mora biti smanjena. Upravo zato nije htio da u javnosti ispadne kako mu je netko „velikodušno nešto dao“.

Opisuje i ozračje suđenja. U prvom stupnju sudac i tužitelj bili su Englezi, kao i svjedoci iz UNPROFOR-a, a obranu su činili američki odvjetnici i hrvatski dio tima. Petočlanim žalbenim vijećem predsjedao je Nijemac.

Predsjednik vijeća pročitao je da mu se **skida sedam od 21 točke**, među njima Busovača i Novi Travnik, ali ne i Ahmići. Po logici stvari, kaže Kordić, kazna je trebala biti smanjena za trećinu, kao što je to, tvrdi, bivalo svakome dok je postojao Haaški sud. Sudac je ipak izrekao: **„Unatoč tome vaša kazna ostaje 25 godina.“**

Kordić se, kako kaže, u sebi „blago raspio“, a supruga je pustila suzu. Ona je znala za što je on molio Gospu. Kao majka i supruga koja se borila s djecom, sve je doživljavala teže.

Zatim je počelo čekanje na to koliko će još ostati u Haagu. Ostale Hrvate koji nisu bili na njegovu katu viđao je samo na misama. Tako je, godinu dana prije svog odlaska iz Haaga, na nekoliko misa vidio i **generala Gotovinu**. S Hrvatima s istog kata družio se u šetnji i dnevnom boravku.

magisterium.assessment: Molitva Gospi za zagovor, uz izričito prihvaćanje Božje volje, u skladu je s katoličkom vjerom: Marija se zaziva kao majka koja posreduje, dok se povjerenje konačno polaže u Boga. Odlomak ponajprije prenosi osobni doživljaj i očekivanje ishoda suđenja, a ne iznosi tvrdnju koja bi proturječila Svetom pismu ili nauku Crkve.
concerns: Izraz „nemoj da mi mrvice sa stola daju“ može zvučati ogorčeno ili kao očekivanje određenog sudskog ishoda, ali sam po sebi ne pokazuje odbacivanje Božje volje ni nauka Crkve.
Spominjanje Međugorja ovdje je naziv u osobnoj pobožnosti; iz ovog odlomka ne može se zaključiti ništa o vjerodostojnosti pojedinih ukazanja.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko zazivanje Marije ne znači da ona djeluje neovisno o Kristu: Crkva njezin zagovor razumije kao majčinsko posredovanje koje vodi Kristu i počiva na njegovu djelovanju. U evanđeoskom primjeru svadbe u Kani Marija iznosi ljudsku potrebu, a potom prepušta ishod Isusu; sličan obrazac povjerenja vidi se i u ovoj molitvi, gdje se molba povezuje s prihvaćanjem Božje volje.

citations.document_title: Mater Populi fidelis - Doctrinal Note on Some Marian Titles Regarding Mary’s Cooperation in the Work of Salvation (4 November 2025)
citations.document_author: Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith

magisterium.assessment_en: A prayer to Our Lady for intercession, with the explicit acceptance of God's will, is in accordance with the Catholic faith: Mary is invoked as an interceding mother, while trust is ultimately placed in God. The passage primarily conveys a personal experience and expectation of the trial's outcome, and does not make a claim that would contradict Sacred Scripture or the teaching of the Church.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic invocation of Mary does not mean that she acts independently of Christ: the Church understands her intercession as maternal mediation that leads to Christ and rests upon his action. In the Gospel example of the wedding at Cana, Mary presents human need and then leaves the outcome to Jesus; a similar pattern of trust is seen in this prayer as well, where the petition is linked to the acceptance of God's will.
concerns_en: The expression “do not let them give me crumbs from the table” may sound bitter or like an expectation of a specific judicial outcome, but in itself it does not show a rejection of God's will or the teaching of the Church.
The mention of Međugorje here is a designation in personal devotion; nothing can be concluded from this passage regarding the authenticity of individual apparitions.

sections.subtitle_en: “Our Lady, do not let them give me crumbs from the table”: appeals verdict without reduction
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest describes his cry to Our Lady of Međugorje before the reading of the appeals verdict
sections.content_en:
Entering the courtroom for the pronunciation of the final verdict, Kordić, as he says, cried out to the **Mother of Međugorje** for the only time: “Our Lady, hear me, but let it be God's will again. Do not let them give me crumbs from the table.” He felt that the defense had submitted so much evidence that his sentence had to be reduced. Precisely because of that, he did not want it to appear in public as though someone had “generously given him something”.

He also describes the atmosphere of the trial. In the first instance, the judge and prosecutor were English, as were the witnesses from UNPROFOR, while the defense consisted of American lawyers and the Croatian part of the team. The five-member appeals chamber was presided over by a German.

The presiding judge of the chamber read out that **seven of the 21 counts were dropped**, among them Busovača and Novi Travnik, but not Ahmići. By the logic of things, Kordić says, the sentence should have been reduced by a third, as was, he claims, the case for everyone while the Hague Tribunal existed. The judge nevertheless pronounced: **“Despite that, your sentence remains 25 years.”**

Kordić, as he says, “gently broke down” inside, and his wife shed a tear. She knew what he had prayed to Our Lady for. As a mother and wife who struggled with the children, she experienced everything more difficultly.

Then began the waiting for how much longer he would remain in The Hague. He saw the other Croats who were not on his floor only at Masses. Thus, a year before his departure from The Hague, he also saw **General Gotovina** at several Masses. With the Croats from the same floor, he spent time on walks and in the common room.

sections.subtitle: Iz Haaga u Graz: zatvor u „Ulici Božje Poljane“ i oklada koju su zatvorenici izgubili
sections.screenshot_description: Dario Kordić opisuje dolazak u zatvor Karlau i veliku sobu s osam zatvorenika
sections.content:
Nakon gotovo **punih devet godina** u pritvoru u Haagu, Dario Kordić upućen je na izdržavanje kazne u jednu od europskih država koje su s Međunarodnim sudom za bivšu Jugoslaviju potpisale sporazum o izvršenju kazni. Upravnik ga je pitao ima li želju kamo bi otišao. Mogao je spomenuti sestru u Njemačkoj, no Kordić je, kako kaže, odgovor prepustio Bogu: „Gospodine, gdje ti misliš da je najbolje, pošalji me.“

Poslan je u zatvor najbliži Hrvatskoj, **Karlau u Grazu**. Sam ističe da se zatvor nalazi u ulici Herrgottwiesgasse, što prevodi kao **Ulica Božje Poljane**. Nakon samice u kojoj je, kako kaže, bio „sa Gospodinom“, smješten je u najveću sobu u tom zatvoru, sa sedmero zatvorenika s raznih kontinenata. Među njima je bio i jedan Hrvat koji ga je dočekao.

Cimeri su već prvoga dana, bez njegova znanja, otvorili **kladionicu**. Okladili su se da će novi zatvorenik izdržati najviše 30 dana, a onda zatražiti premještaj ondje gdje nema dima, droge i tučnjava. Mjesec je prošao, a Kordić je u toj sobi ostao još osam godina. Kroz nju je, prema njegovu računu, prošlo **91 zatvorenika**. Ističe da nikada nije doživio ni ružan pogled, a kamoli nešto gore.

### Krunica i sveta voda među pripadnicima drugih vjera

Među cimerima bilo je malo katolika, a mnogo Arapa i muslimana. Kordić je svakoga od njih ujutro blagoslivljao svetom vodom, javno i pred svima, i nitko mu nikada nije prigovorio. Nakon petnaestak dana zatvorenici su sami počeli dolaziti s molbama: „Dario, hoćeš se pomoliti za ovo ili ono?“ Dok su oni za stolom kockali, „kao u filmovima“, on je šetao s krunicom i molio za svakoga od njih. Naglašava da je toj molitvi pristupao odgovorno i da nikoga tko ga je zamolio nikada nije odbio.

magisterium.assessment: Opis povjeravanja odluke Bogu i molitva za zatvorenike u skladu su s kršćanskim pouzdanjem u Božju providnost te poštovanjem dostojanstva osoba u zatvoru. Ipak, riječ je uglavnom o osobnom svjedočanstvu, a ne o sustavnom izlaganju nauka, pa sam ulomak ne razrađuje odnos Božje providnosti prema ljudskoj slobodi i pravednom izvršavanju kazne.
concerns: Izraz da je određeno mjesto bilo ono gdje ga je Bog „poslao” može se razumjeti kao osobni način govora o pouzdanju; ne bi ga trebalo tumačiti kao dokaz da je Bog izravno odredio svaki pojedini ishod ili da je zatvorska kazna sama po sebi znak posebne Božje volje.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko razumijevanje providnosti dopušta da se čovjek s povjerenjem moli i predaje Bogu ono što ne može kontrolirati, ali istodobno priznaje da Božji naum poštuje ljudsku slobodu i ostaje djelomice otajstven. Zatvorenici, neovisno o počinjenom djelu, ostaju osobe dostojne poštovanja, pastoralne skrbi i nade u obraćenje; milosrđe ne ukida istinu ni pravdu.

citations.document_title: To chaplains of Italian prisons (November 24, 1983) - Speech
Pastoral Visit to Rebibbia Prison - Rome (December 18, 2011)

magisterium.assessment_en: The description of entrusting the decision to God and prayer for prisoners are in accordance with Christian trust in Divine Providence and respect for the dignity of persons in prison. Nevertheless, this is mainly a personal testimony, and not a systematic exposition of teaching, so the passage itself does not elaborate on the relationship of Divine Providence to human freedom and the just execution of punishment.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic understanding of providence allows man to pray with trust and surrender to God what he cannot control, but at the same time recognizes that God's plan respects human freedom and remains partly mysterious. Prisoners, regardless of the act committed, remain persons worthy of respect, pastoral care, and hope for conversion; mercy does not abolish truth or justice.
concerns_en: The expression that a certain place was where God „sent“ him can be understood as a personal way of speaking about trust; it should not be interpreted as proof that God directly determined every single outcome or that a prison sentence in itself is a sign of God's special will.

sections.subtitle_en: From The Hague to Graz: Prison on "God's Field Street" and the Bet the Prisoners Lost
sections.screenshot_description_en: Dario Kordić describes arriving at Karlau prison and the large room with eight prisoners
sections.content_en:
After almost **full nine years** in detention in The Hague, Dario Kordić was sent to serve his sentence in one of the European states that had signed an agreement on the enforcement of sentences with the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia. The warden asked him if he had a wish where he would go. He could have mentioned his sister in Germany, but Kordić, as he says, left the answer to God: „Lord, wherever you think is best, send me.“

He was sent to the prison closest to Croatia, **Karlau in Graz**. He himself points out that the prison is located on Herrgottwiesgasse street, which he translates as **God's Field Street**. After solitary confinement in which, as he says, he was „with the Lord“, he was placed in the largest room in that prison, with seven prisoners from various continents. Among them was also a Croat who welcomed him.

The roommates opened a **betting pool** on the very first day, without his knowledge. They bet that the new prisoner would last at most 30 days, and then request a transfer to where there is no smoke, drugs, and fights. A month passed, and Kordić stayed in that room for another eight years. Through it, according to his count, passed **91 prisoners**. He emphasizes that he never experienced even an ugly look, let alone something worse.

### The Rosary and Holy Water Among Members of Other Faiths

Among the roommates there were few Catholics, and many Arabs and Muslims. In the morning, Kordić blessed each of them with holy water, publicly and in front of everyone, and no one ever objected. After about fifteen days, the prisoners began coming on their own with requests: „Dario, will you pray for this or that?“ While they gambled at the table, „like in movies“, he walked with the Rosary and prayed for each of them. He emphasizes that he approached this prayer responsibly and that he never refused anyone who asked him.
entities_en: International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia

sections.subtitle: Dvije i pol godine molitve: kako je slika vraga ustupila mjesto Lurdskoj Gospi
sections.screenshot_description: Dario Kordić pripovijeda kako je cimer poderao sliku vraga i zatražio sliku Gospe
sections.content:
Voditelj Krunoslav podsjeća gosta na jedno svjedočanstvo iz Graza koje je Kordić, kako sam kaže, često pričao: priču o dvije slike, Gospinoj i Sotoninoj.

Kordić najprije opisuje posljednjih pet godina zatočeništva, provedenih uglavnom s ljudima s prostora bivše države. Hrvata gotovo nije bilo, nego su to većinom bili **Srbi, muslimani i Albanci**. Upravo s njima, ističe, provodio je Božiće koji su mu ostali posebni. Pripremali bi mu ih, a on bi odlazio na ponoćku koja se služila danju, u crkvi na njegovu katu. Kasnije bi u sobi upalio svijeće, a cimeri bi ustali i molili zajedno s njim, „s punim poštovanjem“. Tog se vremena, kaže, sjeća s radošću, iako je, „kao i u svakoj sobi“, bilo svega i svačega.

Iznad svog željeznog kreveta imao je:
- **križ**,
- **sliku Presvetoga Trojstva**,
- **fotografiju svoje obitelji**,
- **sliku Lurdske Gospe** koju su mu s hodočašća poslali hrvatski branitelji, slika koja se mijenja ovisno o kutu gledanja.

Tada je u sobu došao zatvorenik koji je na ormar, osamdesetak do sto centimetara od Kordićeva uzglavlja, zalijepio veliku i iznimno ružnu sliku vraga. Sobe su bile pod reflektorima pa je pogled na nju bio neizbježan, i noću pri odlasku u toalet i ujutro pri buđenju.

Kordić tom zatvoreniku nikada ništa nije rekao jer je, kako objašnjava, to bio njegov prostor i njegov ormar. Umjesto toga **ustrajno je molio** da mu Bog dotakne srce. Nakon otprilike **dvije i pol godine** cimer ga je jednog poslijepodneva pozvao pred svima i rekao: „Dario, vrijeme je da ovaj đavo ide s ovoga.“ Sliku je poderao jednom, zatim još jednom, bacio je u koš te upitao bi li mu Kordić dao sliku Gospe da je zalijepi na isto mjesto. Gospina slika ondje je ostala do kraja Kordićeva zatočeništva.

„Pa samo da sam to doživio, a doživio sam stotine još drugih stvari“, zaključuje Kordić, uvjeren da je Božja ruka vodila svaki trenutak njegova boravka u zatvoru.

magisterium.assessment: Opis je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim naukom: ustrajna molitva, marijanska pobožnost i kršćansko svjedočanstvo u zatvoru mogu biti izrazi vjere i nade, a prijateljski odnos sa zatvorenicima drugih vjera nije u suprotnosti s katoličanstvom. Budući da je prikazan samo sažetak, nije moguće procijeniti što se točno misli tvrdnjom da je slika vraga ustupila mjesto Lurdskoj Gospi.
concerns: Ako se promjena slika prikazuje kao nadnaravni znak ili kao učinak koji molitva automatski jamči, takvu bi tvrdnju trebalo pažljivo razlučiti; sam sažetak ne pruža dovoljno pojedinosti da bi se utvrdilo iznosi li se takvo tumačenje.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolička vjera ozbiljno govori o Sotoni, ali ga ne stavlja u središte evanđeoske poruke: središte pripada Bogu i Kristovoj pobjedi. Marijanska pobožnost može podupirati molitvu i pouzdanje u Boga, ali ne zamjenjuje Krista niti djeluje kao magijski mehanizam; osobna svjedočanstva o duhovnim iskustvima valja razlikovati od obvezujućeg nauka Crkve.
