citations.document_author: Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith

magisterium.assessment_en: The description is largely aligned with Catholic teaching: persistent prayer, Marian devotion, and Christian witness in prison can be expressions of faith and hope, and a friendly relationship with prisoners of other faiths is not contrary to Catholicism. Since only a summary is presented, it is not possible to assess what exactly is meant by the claim that the image of the devil gave way to Our Lady of Lourdes.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic faith speaks seriously about Satan, but does not place him at the center of the gospel message: the center belongs to God and Christ's victory. Marian devotion can support prayer and trust in God, but does not replace Christ nor act as a magical mechanism; personal testimonies of spiritual experiences must be distinguished from the binding teaching of the Church.
concerns_en: If the change of images is presented as a supernatural sign or as an effect automatically guaranteed by prayer, such a claim should be carefully discerned; the summary itself does not provide enough details to determine whether such an interpretation is being made.

sections.subtitle_en: Two and a half years of prayer: how the image of the devil gave way to Our Lady of Lourdes
sections.screenshot_description_en: Dario Kordić recounts how his roommate tore up the image of the devil and asked for an image of Our Lady
sections.content_en:
Host Krunoslav reminds the guest of a testimony from Graz that Kordić, as he says himself, often told: the story of two images, Our Lady's and Satan's.

Kordić first describes the last five years of his captivity, spent mostly with people from the territory of the former state. There were almost no Croats, but rather they were mostly **Serbs, Muslims, and Albanians**. It was precisely with them, he emphasizes, that he spent Christmases that remained special to him. They would prepare them for him, and he would go to Midnight Mass, which was celebrated during the day, in the church on his floor. Later, he would light candles in the room, and his roommates would stand up and pray together with him, „with full respect“. That time, he says, he remembers with joy, although, „as in every room“, there was a bit of everything.

Above his iron bed he had:
- **a cross**,
- **an image of the Most Holy Trinity**,
- **a photograph of his family**,
- **an image of Our Lady of Lourdes** that Croatian veterans had sent him from a pilgrimage, an image that changes depending on the viewing angle.

Then a prisoner came into the room who taped a large and extremely ugly image of the devil onto a wardrobe, about eighty to a hundred centimeters from Kordić's headboard. The rooms were under floodlights, so looking at it was unavoidable, both at night when going to the toilet and in the morning upon waking up.

Kordić never said anything to that prisoner because, as he explains, it was his space and his wardrobe. Instead, **he persistently prayed** that God would touch his heart. After about **two and a half years**, one afternoon his roommate called him in front of everyone and said: „Dario, it is time for this devil to go from this.“ He tore the image once, then once more, threw it into the trash bin, and asked if Kordić would give him an image of Our Lady to tape in the same spot. The image of Our Lady remained there until the end of Kordić's captivity.

„Even if I had only experienced that, and I experienced hundreds of other things besides“, concludes Kordić, convinced that God's hand guided every moment of his stay in prison.

sections.subtitle: Venera i troje djece: život od Božje providnosti
sections.screenshot_description: Dario Kordić govori o tome kako je supruga Venera preživljavala oslanjajući se na Božju providnost
sections.content:
Krunoslav potom pita kako je bez muža živjela **Venera** s troje male djece. Napominje da je u početku uživala određena prava, a da su kasnije i ta prava i novac izostali.

Kordić objašnjava da je obitelj, dok je bio živ predsjednik **Tuđman**, imala sve potrebno, i od Hrvatske i od Bosne i Hercegovine. Potpora Hrvata iz BiH trajala je do upada tenkova u **Hercegovačku banku**, oko 2002. godine. Kordić ističe da te događaje zna samo iz medija jer tada nije bio na slobodi. Nakon toga su prestale i te mogućnosti.

Od tog trenutka, kaže Kordić, supruga počinje živjeti „od **Božje providnosti**“. Mnogo puta mu je svjedočila kako bi otišla pred Presveto ili u malu kapelicu svetog Ante na Svetom Duhu i zavapila Gospodinu. Ne bi prošlo ni 24 sata, a njezine bi materijalne potrebe bile riješene, i to preko ljudi od kojih to nitko ne bi očekivao. Kordić iz toga izvlači i osobnu pouku: ne treba se uzdati u ljude za koje misliš da ti nešto duguju, jer pomoć često dolazi od nekoga koga uopće ne poznaješ.

### Odojak i bor s Trešnjevačkog placa

Kao ilustraciju supružine vjere Kordić navodi jednu anegdotu. Bilo je vrijeme Božića, a u kući su sjedili kumovi pred kojima je Venera često ponavljala „Božja providnost“. Kum se našalio: „Pa hajde sad, sad će tebi netko doći, pokucati na vrata i donijeti odojak i bor.“

Ubrzo je zazvonilo. Na vratima je stajao čovjek s **Trešnjevačkog placa**: „Ja sam ovdje poslan, je li ovdje živi supruga Darija Kordića? Moj gazda je poslao bor, poslao odojak, poslao ovo, ono.“ Kordić naglašava da je to bilo svjedočanstvo upravo za kumove koji su sjedili za stolom, jer supruzi, kako kaže, takav dokaz nije ni trebao.

magisterium.assessment: U prikazanom ulomku nema izričite tvrdnje koja bi bila protivna katoličkom nauku; opis pomoći obitelji u oskudici u skladu je s kršćanskom dužnošću skrbi za obitelji i potrebite. Ipak, ulomak je prekinut, pa se ne može procijeniti kako se u nastavku povezuju Božja providnost i materijalna potpora.
magisterium.enrichment: Vjera u Božju providnost poziva na pouzdanje u Boga, ali ne znači obećanje da će svaka obitelj uvijek imati osigurana materijalna dobra; Crkva također naglašava konkretno djelovanje i pomoć ljudima u potrebi. Papa Franjo ističe da siromaštvo može teško opteretiti obiteljske veze te da kršćani trebaju biti blizu obiteljima koje prolaze kušnju, a Pio XI. potvrđuje dužnost pomaganja kada obitelji nedostaju nužna sredstva.

citations.document_title: General Audience of 3 June 2015: The family - 17. Family and poverty

magisterium.assessment_en: In the presented excerpt there is no explicit claim that would be contrary to Catholic teaching; the description of help to a family in scarcity is in accordance with the Christian duty of caring for families and the needy. Nevertheless, the excerpt is interrupted, so it cannot be assessed how God's providence and material support are connected in what follows.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Faith in God's providence calls for trust in God, but does not mean a promise that every family will always have material goods provided; the Church also emphasizes concrete action and help to people in need. Pope Francis points out that poverty can heavily burden family ties and that Christians should be close to families going through trial, and Pius XI confirms the duty of helping when a family lacks necessary means.

sections.subtitle_en: Venera and three children: living off God's providence
sections.screenshot_description_en: Dario Kordić speaks about how his wife Venera survived by relying on God's providence
sections.content_en:
Krunoslav then asks how **Venera** lived without a husband with three small children. He notes that at the beginning she enjoyed certain rights, and that later both those rights and money ceased.

Kordić explains that the family, while President **Tuđman** was alive, had everything necessary, both from Croatia and from Bosnia and Herzegovina. The support of Croats from BiH lasted until the raid of tanks into **Hercegovačka banka**, around the year 2002. Kordić points out that he knows those events only from the media because he was not free at that time. After that, those possibilities also ceased.

From that moment, Kordić says, his wife begins to live "on **God's providence**". She testified to him many times how she would go before the Blessed Sacrament or into the small chapel of Saint Anthony on Sveti Duh and cry out to the Lord. Not even 24 hours would pass, and her material needs would be resolved, and that through people from whom no one would expect it. Kordić also draws a personal lesson from this: one should not rely on people whom you think owe you something, because help often comes from someone you do not know at all.

### Suckling pig and Christmas tree from Trešnjevački plac

As an illustration of his wife's faith, Kordić cites an anecdote. It was Christmas time, and godparents were sitting in the house before whom Venera often repeated "God's providence". The godfather joked: "Well come on now, now someone will come to you, knock on the door, and bring a suckling pig and a Christmas tree."

Soon the doorbell rang. At the door stood a man from **Trešnjevački plac**: "I was sent here, does the wife of Dario Kordić live here? My boss sent a Christmas tree, sent a suckling pig, sent this, that." Kordić emphasizes that this was a testimony precisely for the godparents who were sitting at the table, because his wife, as he says, did not even need such proof.

sections.subtitle: „Ja želim doći“: posao u Alfi i majka koja je bila i otac
sections.screenshot_description: Dario Kordić opisuje suprugin prvi radni dan, kad je pješice kroz snijeg došla na posao
sections.content:
Zahvaljujući dobrim ljudima, Venera je dobila posao u **Alfi**. Kordić ističe da je vlasnik tvrtke pokazao veliko srce. Ponudio joj je plaću bez obveze dolaska na posao: „Hajde dođi, Venera, pa ti budi ovdje, davat ćemo ti plaću. Ne moraš ni raditi.“ Ona je ponudu odbila riječima: „Ja nisam na to naučila, ja želim doći.“

Prvi radni dan u Zagrebu je napadalo **70 centimetara snijega**. Venera je od Trešnjevke do radnog mjesta na Novoj vesi došla pješice i bila je jedina zaposlenica koja se toga dana pojavila. Kordić dodaje da i danas radi u školstvu, u istoj izdavačkoj kući, i da se bori „s osmijehom na licu“. Opisuje je kao **najveseliju ženu na svijetu**, kojoj nitko nikada nije mogao vidjeti na licu koliko je patila.

### Odgoj bez oca

Patnja je ipak bila stvarna. Venera je, kaže Kordić, morala biti i otac i majka, i sinu i kćerima. Posebno je teško bilo sa sinom u adolescenciji, koji je poput mnogih mladića prolazio kroz sve izazove toga doba, a uz to je s **Bad Blue Boysima** putovao po Europi. U detalje Kordić ne želi ulaziti i kaže samo da je „sve to iza nas“.

Molitvom je, ističe, Gospodin sve okrenuo nabolje. Kad se vratio iz zatvora, troje djece već je bilo na putu da postanu obiteljski ljudi, a danas to i jesu. Najmlađa kći imala je tek nešto više od godine dana kada je otišao u Haag. On je stigao na njezin **maturalni ples 2014. godine**, nedugo nakon izlaska iz zatvora.

magisterium.assessment: Opis Venerina odbijanja plaće bez rada i njezine spremnosti da radi uglavnom je usklađen s katoličkim poimanjem rada kao služenja obitelji i sudjelovanja u zajedničkom dobru. Prikaz njezine ustrajnosti može svjedočiti o dostojanstvu rada, ali iz samog odlomka nije moguće procijeniti šire tvrdnje o Božjoj providnosti ili životu svjedočanstva.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički nauk ističe da rad pridonosi uzdržavanju i stabilnosti obitelji te da radom čovjek razvija svoje darove i služi društvu; zato Venerina želja da pošteno radi ima razumljiv kršćanski smisao. Ipak, dostojanstvo osobe ne ovisi o tome može li raditi: pomoć bez zahtjeva za radom može biti izraz velikodušnosti, a nezaposlenost ne umanjuje ljudsku vrijednost.
magisterium.assessment_en: The description of Venera's refusal of a salary without work and her readiness to work is largely aligned with the Catholic understanding of work as service to the family and participation in the common good. The portrayal of her perseverance can bear witness to the dignity of work, but from the excerpt itself it is not possible to assess broader claims about God's providence or a life of witness.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic teaching emphasizes that work contributes to the sustenance and stability of the family and that through work man develops his gifts and serves society; therefore, Venera's desire to work honestly has an understandable Christian meaning. Nevertheless, the dignity of the person does not depend on whether one can work: help without the requirement to work can be an expression of generosity, and unemployment does not diminish human worth.

sections.subtitle_en: "I want to come": a job at Alfa and a mother who was also a father
sections.screenshot_description_en: Dario Kordić describes his wife's first working day, when she came to work on foot through the snow
sections.content_en:
Thanks to good people, Venera got a job at **Alfa**. Kordić emphasizes that the owner of the company showed a big heart. He offered her a salary without the obligation of coming to work: "Come on, Venera, just be here, we will give you a salary. You don't even have to work." She refused the offer with the words: "I am not used to that, I want to come."

On the first working day, **70 centimeters of snow** fell in Zagreb. Venera walked from Trešnjevka to her workplace in Nova ves on foot and was the only employee who showed up that day. Kordić adds that today she still works in education, in the same publishing house, and that she fights "with a smile on her face." He describes her as **the most cheerful woman in the world**, on whose face no one could ever see how much she suffered.

### Upbringing without a father

The suffering was nevertheless real. Venera, says Kordić, had to be both a father and a mother, both to the son and the daughters. It was especially difficult with the son in adolescence, who, like many young men, went through all the challenges of that age, and in addition traveled around Europe with the **Bad Blue Boys**. Kordić does not want to go into details and only says that "all of that is behind us."

Through prayer, he emphasizes, the Lord turned everything for the better. When he returned from prison, three children were already on their way to becoming family people, and today they are. The youngest daughter was only a little over a year old when he left for The Hague. He arrived at her **prom in 2014**, shortly after his release from prison.

sections.subtitle: „Slobodniji u rešetkama nego svi ljudi na svijetu“
sections.screenshot_description: Dario Kordić objašnjava zašto se u zatvoru osjećao slobodnije nego danas
sections.content:
Govoreći o dvanaest godina provedenih na slobodi, Kordić iznosi tvrdnju koja na prvi pogled zvuči paradoksalno: „Ja uvijek kažem, ja sam slobodniji bio u rešetkama od svih ljudi na svijetu. Ja sam bio najslobodniji tada. Ova mi je sloboda manje slobodna nego ona iz zatvora.“

Supruga ga, priznaje, zna zadirkivati da „s čežnjom gleda na ono zatvoreničko vrijeme“. Kordić to slikovito objašnjava: u zatvoru bi ujutro u miru skuhao čaj i uzeo meda, dok u današnjem dnevnom ritmu „nema ni čajeva, ni medova, samo te lomi“.

### Povratak na petak, dan križa

Krunoslav pita je li se vratio **6. lipnja**. Kordić potvrđuje i ističe da mu je posebno drago što je to bio **petak**, dan Isusove muke i križa. Tu iznosi i jedno od svojih životnih načela:

> „Ja ljubim taj križ Isusov i kad nešto previše dobro ide na ovom životu, ja se zabrinem. Dok pljuju, dok napadaju, dok nešto je teško, ja kažem: Hvala ti, Bože, na tvom smo putu.“

magisterium.assessment: Tvrdnja da je u zatvoru bio „slobodniji” može se razumjeti kao osobno svjedočanstvo o unutarnjoj slobodi koju vjera može dati i u vanjskim ograničenjima, što je u skladu s katoličkim naglaskom na oslobođenju od grijeha po Kristu. Ipak, formulacija je retorička i ne treba je shvatiti kao tvrdnju da je zatvorska kazna poželjnija ili da fizička sloboda nije važna.
concerns: Izjava „slobodniji od svih ljudi na svijetu” široka je osobna hiperbola, a ne opće teološko mjerilo slobode.

Bez dodatnog pojašnjenja postoji mogućnost romantiziranja zatvora ili patnje; katoličko vrednovanje unutarnje slobode ne poništava vrijednost dostojanstva osobe ni opravdanu brigu za pravedne i humane zatvorske uvjete.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko razumijevanje slobode razlikuje vanjsku slobodu od dublje slobode srca: čovjek može biti fizički ograničen, a ipak se, uz Kristovu milost, oslobađati ropstva grijehu i svojih strasti. Ivan Pavao II. zato ističe da se prava unutarnja sloboda može začeti bez obzira na vanjsko stanje, ali i da patnja dobiva smisao u svjetlu Krista, a ne zato što je sama po sebi dobra ili poželjna.

magisterium.assessment_en: The claim that he was „freer” in prison can be understood as a personal testimony of the inner freedom that faith can give even within external limitations, which is in accordance with the Catholic emphasis on liberation from sin through Christ. Nevertheless, the formulation is rhetorical and should not be understood as a claim that a prison sentence is preferable or that physical freedom is not important.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic understanding of freedom distinguishes external freedom from the deeper freedom of the heart: man can be physically constrained, and yet, with Christ's grace, be liberated from slavery to sin and one's passions. John Paul II therefore emphasizes that true inner freedom can arise regardless of external conditions, but also that suffering acquires meaning in the light of Christ, and not because it is good or desirable in itself.
concerns_en: The statement „freer than all the people in the world” is a broad personal hyperbole, and not a general theological standard of freedom.

Without additional clarification, there is a possibility of romanticizing prison or suffering; the Catholic appreciation of inner freedom does not negate the value of the dignity of the person nor the justified concern for just and humane prison conditions.

sections.subtitle_en: „Freer behind bars than all the people in the world“
sections.screenshot_description_en: Dario Kordić explains why he felt freer in prison than today
sections.content_en:
Speaking about the twelve years spent in freedom, Kordić makes a claim that at first glance sounds paradoxical: „I always say, I was freer behind bars than all the people in the world. I was the freest then. This freedom to me is less free than the one from prison.“

His wife, he admits, sometimes teases him that he „looks back with longing at that prison time“. Kordić explains this vividly: in prison, in the morning he would brew tea and have honey in peace, while in today's daily rhythm „there is neither tea nor honey, it just breaks you“.

### Return on Friday, the day of the cross

Krunoslav asks if he returned on **June 6**. Kordić confirms and emphasizes that he is especially pleased that it was a **Friday**, the day of Jesus' passion and cross. Here he also presents one of his life principles:

> „I love that cross of Jesus and when something goes too well in this life, I get worried. While they spit, while they attack, while something is difficult, I say: Thank you, God, we are on your path.“

sections.subtitle: Bez zahtjeva za pomilovanje: izlet u Mariazell i sveti Bernard na slici
sections.screenshot_description: Dario Kordić opisuje sliku svetog Bernarda čija se glava spaja s glavom raspetog Krista
sections.content:
Krunoslav zatim pita gosta za odlazak u **Mariazell** dok je bio u Grazu. Kordić prije odgovora otkriva odluku koju je, kako kaže, donio samostalno, „dok je bio pri pameti“: **nikada neće podnijeti zahtjev za pomilovanje**. „Kad bude Božja volja, izaći ću.“

Prema njegovim riječima, Bog je nadahnuo ljude iz **austrijskog pravosuđa**. Oni su u dva navrata pisali da „ovaj čovjek više kod nas u Austriji ne treba biti“, a Kordić te dopise i danas čuva. Iz Haaga je stigao odgovor da je „rano“. Godine 2014., kad je iza sebe imao gotovo 17 godina zatočeništva, posjetila ga je jedna Španjolka iz **Crvenog križa** s viješću da ni tog ljeta nema šanse i da će se o njegovu slučaju odlučivati tek nakon Božića, 2015. godine. Kordić kaže da je to već bio prihvatio.

### Neplanirano zaustavljanje

Tada mu je zatvorski dušobrižnik (*Seelsorger*) javio da je zajedno s još četvoricom zatvorenika određen za **socijalni izlazak**, na svetu misu u Mariazellu, uz stražu i u lisicama. Vožnja je trajala, prisjeća se, sat i pol do dva.

Usput su stali u gradić za koji Kordić misli da se zvao **Neuberg**. Ondje se nalazi crkva sagrađena po uzoru na staru crkvu iz Njemačke, nekadašnja katedrala i **cistercitski samostan**, danas uglavnom napušten. Među stotinama slika Kordićevu je pažnju privukla jedna: **sveti Bernard** kleči na klecalu pred raspetim Kristom, a njihove su glave umjetnički spojene u jednu.

U tom trenutku, pred kraj zatočeništva, Kordić je u srcu osjetio Gospodinove riječi: to je ono što je izrekao **sveti Pavao**, „ne živim više ja, živi Krist u meni“. Kaže da mu je ta misao često dolazila, a sada mu je Gospodin pokazao njezino značenje.

### „Ideš doma“

U Mariazellu je jedan od slavitelja mise bio **fra Šimun Oreč**, župnik u jednoj austrijskoj župi, koji ga je često posjećivao u zatvoru i kod kojega je Kordić ponekad izlazio. Tijekom mise, kao i onda kad je kod presude zamolio Gospu, u srcu je začuo glas: **„Ideš, ideš doma. Ideš doma.“** Odmah se zapitao kako će ići doma kad su mu upravo rekli da neće.

magisterium.assessment: Odluka da ne traži pomilovanje i povjerenje da će izaći kada bude Božja volja mogu se razumjeti kao osobni čin savjesti i pouzdanja u Providnost, a ne kao opće pravilo za katolike. Uvjerenje da je Bog nadahnuo austrijske pravosudne djelatnike nije samo po sebi protivno nauku, ali ga treba izreći kao osobno tumačenje događaja, a ne kao nešto što se može sa sigurnošću dokazati.
concerns: Moguće je pretjerano pripisivanje konkretnog pravosudnog postupka izravnom Božjem nadahnuću ako se zanemare ljudska prosudba, sloboda i drugi uzroci događaja.

Iz isječka nije jasno predstavlja li odbijanje pomilovanja samo osobni izbor ili se sugerira da bi traženje pomilovanja bilo protivno vjeri; prvo je pitanje osobne odluke, dok za drugo ovdje nema temelja.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko razumijevanje Providnosti dopušta vjerniku da u događajima prepozna Božje vodstvo, ali uobičajeno djelovanje Providnosti ostvaruje se i preko ljudskih odluka i drugih sekundarnih uzroka, bez ukidanja njihove slobode i odgovornosti. Zato je primjereno govoriti o zahvalnom i poniznom tumačenju vlastitog iskustva, uz svijest da se Božji naum ne može uvijek sa sigurnošću iščitati iz pojedinačnog ishoda.

citations.document_reference: The Nature and Attributes of God

magisterium.assessment_en: The decision not to seek a pardon and the trust that he will get out when it is God's will can be understood as a personal act of conscience and reliance on Providence, rather than as a general rule for Catholics. The conviction that God inspired Austrian judicial officials is not in itself contrary to teaching, but it should be expressed as a personal interpretation of events, rather than as something that can be proven with certainty.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic understanding of Providence allows a believer to recognize God's guidance in events, but the ordinary operation of Providence is also realized through human decisions and other secondary causes, without abolishing their freedom and responsibility. Therefore, it is appropriate to speak of a grateful and humble interpretation of one's own experience, with the awareness that God's plan cannot always be read with certainty from an individual outcome.
concerns_en: An excessive attribution of a specific judicial proceeding to direct divine inspiration is possible if human judgment, freedom, and other causes of events are disregarded.

It is not clear from the excerpt whether the refusal of a pardon represents only a personal choice or if it suggests that seeking a pardon would be contrary to faith; the former is a matter of personal decision, whereas for the latter there is no basis here.

sections.subtitle_en: Without a Request for Pardon: A Trip to Mariazell and Saint Bernard in a Painting
sections.screenshot_description_en: Dario Kordić describes a painting of Saint Bernard whose head merges with the head of the crucified Christ
sections.content_en:
Krunoslav then asks the guest about going to **Mariazell** while he was in Graz. Before answering, Kordić reveals a decision that, as he says, he made independently, "while he was in his right mind": **he will never submit a request for pardon**. "When it is God's will, I will get out."

According to his words, God inspired people from the **Austrian judiciary**. On two occasions they wrote that "this man should no longer be with us in Austria," and Kordić still keeps those letters today. A response arrived from The Hague saying that it was "early." In 2014, when he had nearly 17 years of imprisonment behind him, a Spanish woman from the **Red Cross** visited him with the news that there was no chance that summer either and that his case would be decided only after Christmas, in 2015. Kordić says he had already accepted that.

### An Unplanned Stop

Then the prison chaplain (*Seelsorger*) informed him that, together with four other prisoners, he had been designated for a **social outing**, to Holy Mass in Mariazell, under guard and in handcuffs. The drive lasted, he recalls, an hour and a half to two hours.

Along the way, they stopped in a small town that Kordić thinks was called **Neuberg**. Located there is a church built after the model of an old church from Germany, a former cathedral and **Cistercian monastery**, today mostly abandoned. Among hundreds of paintings, one caught Kordić's attention: **Saint Bernard** kneeling on a kneeler before the crucified Christ, and their heads are artistically merged into one.

At that moment, near the end of his imprisonment, Kordić felt the Lord's words in his heart: that is what **Saint Paul** uttered, "it is no longer I who live, Christ lives in me." He says that this thought often came to him, and now the Lord showed him its meaning.

### "You Are Going Home"

In Mariazell, one of the celebrants of the Mass was **fra Šimun Oreč**, a parish priest in an Austrian parish, who often visited him in prison and to whose place Kordić sometimes went out. During the Mass, just as back when he asked Our Lady at the verdict, he heard a voice in his heart: **"You are going, you are going home. You are going home."** He immediately wondered how he would go home when they had just told him he would not.

sections.subtitle: Posljednja noć u zatvoru, zaustavljeni zrakoplov i Drava ispod krila
sections.screenshot_description: Dario Kordić pripovijeda o posljednjoj noći u zatvoru s Afganistancem i Alžircem
sections.content:
Već sljedećeg dana u njegovu je sobu ušao gospodin **Riedl** s riječima: „Dario, ideš kući.“ Kordić tada nije dobio nikakav papir ni rješenje o izlasku. Službeno rješenje stiglo mu je tek šest mjeseci kasnije. Taj trenutak uspoređuje s oslobađanjem **svetog Petra i svetog Pavla**, kada su se vrata, kako kaže, sama otvarala.

Vijest je saznao u utorak, dok su ga posjećivala trojica Hrvata, a let je bio predviđen za petak. Dušobrižnik ga je upozorio da će ga voziti „jednim jadnim autom“ kroz dvadesetak zatvora, od jutra do mraka, sve do **Beča**. Bio je to dan poplave u **Gunji**. Vladala je velika vrućina, a Kordić je sjedio stisnut uz jednog Mađara, bez vode. Ipak je zahvaljivao Bogu jer su ga sutradan čekali najbliži i već je bila dogovorena sveta misa u crkvi **svetog Josipa na Trešnjevci**.

### Noć s Afganistancem i Alžircem

Kordić se veselio što će posljednju noć provesti s Mađarom, no stražar ga je, nakon što su svjetla već bila ugašena, uveo u drugu sobu i najavio: „Ovaj će zatvorenik moliti se sad Bogu 15–20, pola sata i onda ćemo ugasiti svjetlo.“ Ispod deka dočekali su ga neprijateljski pogledi. Dobio je jedini krevet na kat u sobi.

Razgovor je počeo s mladim **Afganistancem**. Kordić mu je spomenuo da je u zatvoru imao dobrog prijatelja iz Afganistana, a pokazalo se da su njih dvojica prvi rođaci. Mladić mu je odmah ponudio pola svog kreveta i Bibliju da čita kod njega. U isto vrijeme cimer iz **Alžira**, očito u teškom stanju, tresao je krevet na kojem je Kordić trebao spavati i dozivao stražare tražeći ljude iz svoje zemlje. Stražari su ga smirili i tako je, kaže Kordić, „probio tu noć“.

### Križ kao „hladno oružje“

Sljedećeg jutra nije bilo konzula, nije bilo papira ni privremene putovnice. Ponovno je završio u **migracijskom zatvoru**, gdje su mu opet uzeli otiske prstiju i fotografirali ga. Već se pomirio s time da toga dana neće stići u Zagreb. Tada je zadihan stigao konzul, upalila su se rotirajuća svjetla i zrakoplov je zaustavljen. Na ulazu su mu križ oduzeli kao „**hladno oružje**“, a vratili su mu ga kasnije.

Za vrijeme leta pratio je zemljopis ispod sebe. Kad je ugledao **Dravu**, znao je da ulazi u Hrvatsku. „I to je sve ostalo onda povijest“, kaže.

magisterium.assessment: Usporedba vlastitog izlaska iz zatvora s oslobođenjem svetog Petra i Pavla može se razumjeti kao osobno svjedočanstvo o Božjoj providnosti te je u tom smislu spojiva s katoličkom vjerom. Ipak, biblijski izvještaji opisuju različite događaje: Petru se željezna vrata otvaraju sama od sebe, dok se zatvorska vrata za Pavla i Silu otvaraju nakon potresa.
concerns: Usporedba bi mogla zamagliti razliku između osobnog tumačenja događaja kao providencijalnog i tvrdnje da se dogodilo čudo u istom smislu kao u Djelima apostolskim; dostupni ulomak ne pokazuje jasno tvrdi li se takvo izjednačavanje.
magisterium.enrichment: Dj 12 prikazuje Petra oslobođenog nakon što Crkva ustrajno moli, a pripovijest izričito kaže da su se željezna vrata otvorila sama od sebe. U Dj 16 potres otvara vrata tamnice u kojoj su Pavao i Sila, ali oni ne bježe; Pavao potom traži da ih vlasti javno izvedu jer su bili nezakonito kažnjeni. Katoličko tumačenje zato može prepoznati Božju blizinu i djelovanje providnosti, a da se pritom ne pretpostavi kako svaki povoljan ishod mora biti čudesna intervencija.

magisterium.assessment_en: The comparison of one's own release from prison with the liberation of Saints Peter and Paul can be understood as a personal testimony of God's providence and is in that sense compatible with the Catholic faith. Nevertheless, the biblical accounts describe different events: for Peter, the iron gate opens on its own, whereas the prison doors for Paul and Silas open after an earthquake.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Acts 12 shows Peter delivered after the Church prays perseveringly, and the narrative explicitly states that the iron gate opened on its own. In Acts 16, an earthquake opens the doors of the prison in which Paul and Silas are held, but they do not flee; Paul subsequently demands that the authorities bring them out publicly because they were punished unlawfully. Catholic interpretation can therefore recognize God's closeness and the action of providence without presuming that every favorable outcome must be a miraculous intervention.
concerns_en: The comparison could blur the distinction between a personal interpretation of events as providential and a claim that a miracle occurred in the same sense as in the Acts of the Apostles; the available excerpt does not clearly show whether such an equation is being claimed.

sections.subtitle_en: The last night in prison, a stopped airplane, and the Drava beneath the wings
sections.screenshot_description_en: Dario Kordić recounts the last night in prison with an Afghan and an Algerian
sections.content_en:
Already the following day, Mr. **Riedl** entered his room with the words: "Dario, you are going home." Kordić at that time received no paper or decision regarding his release. The official decision arrived to him only six months later. He compares that moment with the liberation of **Saint Peter and Saint Paul**, when the doors, as he says, opened on their own.

He learned the news on Tuesday, while three Croats were visiting him, and the flight was scheduled for Friday. The pastoral minister warned him that they would drive him in "a miserable car" through some twenty prisons, from morning to dark, all the way to **Beč**. It was the day of the flood in **Gunja**. Great heat prevailed, and Kordić sat squeezed next to a Hungarian, without water. Still, he thanked God because the next day his closest ones were waiting for him and a holy Mass had already been arranged in the church of **Saint Joseph in Trešnjevka**.

### A night with an Afghan and an Algerian

Kordić was looking forward to spending the last night with the Hungarian, but the guard, after the lights had already been turned off, brought him into another room and announced: "This prisoner will pray to God now for 15–20, half an hour, and then we will turn off the light." Hostile glances met him from under the blankets. He was given the only bunk bed in the room.

The conversation began with a young **Afghan**. Kordić mentioned to him that he had a good friend from Afghanistan in prison, and it turned out that the two of them were first cousins. The young man immediately offered him half of his bed and the Bible to read at his place. At the same time, the roommate from **Algeria**, visibly in a difficult state, was shaking the bed on which Kordić was supposed to sleep and calling out to the guards, asking for people from his country. The guards calmed him down and thus, says Kordić, he "broke through that night."

### The cross as a "cold weapon"

The next morning there was no consul, there were no papers or temporary passport. He ended up again in the **migration prison**, where they took his fingerprints again and photographed him. He had already resigned himself to the fact that he would not arrive in Zagreb that day. Then the consul arrived out of breath, the rotating lights turned on, and the airplane was stopped. At the entrance, they took his cross away as a "**cold weapon**", and returned it to him later.

During the flight, he followed the geography beneath him. When he caught sight of the **Drava**, he knew he was entering Croatia. "And all the rest of that then is history," he says.

sections.subtitle: Zavjet ispunjen u 60. godini: od „teologije na koljenima“ do diplome
sections.screenshot_description: Dario Kordić govori o zavjetu da upiše studij teologije ako izađe iz zatvora
sections.content:
Krunoslav primjećuje da je Kordić tih 17 godina zapravo „studirao teologiju na koljenima“, a ipak je iste godine kad je izašao upisao i formalni studij teologije. Pita je li to bio zavjet.

Kordić potvrđuje da jest. Kad je u zatvoru osjetio duhovni poziv, obećao je Gospodinu: ako bude imao priliku živjeti izvan zatvorskih zidina, upisat će taj studij. Kroz šalu dodaje da to nije učinio zato što nije imao što drugo raditi.

Bio je, kaže, **revan student**. U pet godina studija izostao je samo dva dana, zbog sprovoda. Nije tražio nikakve iznimke: pohađao je i tjelesni odgoj, i obilaske, i sve ostalo što su imali i drugi studenti. Uživao je u studiju i u njemu otkrio mnogo toga što prije nije znao.

Neki su ga ljudi zadirkivali da će „na studiju teologije izgubiti vjeru“. Kordić odgovara da ju je, Bogu hvala, ondje samo **produbio**. Diplomirao je u vrijeme korone, okružen mnogo mladih ljudi. Prvi fakultet završio je 1983. godine, u studentske klupe ponovno je sjeo nakon 31 godine, a drugi je fakultet završio **u 60. godini života**.

magisterium.assessment: Opis osobnog zavjeta i ozbiljnog studija teologije u skladu je s katoličkim razumijevanjem vjere kao poziva na odgovor Bogu, a u odlomku nema očite proturječnosti katoličkom nauku. Iz samog isječka, međutim, nije moguće procijeniti narav ni obvezatnost zavjeta u konkretnom slučaju.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolička tradicija cijeni teološki studij jer pomaže razumjeti cjelinu vjere i obrazložiti kršćansku nadu, a ne samo steći praktično znanje. Istodobno, studij teologije treba ostati povezan s molitvom, poniznošću i ljubavlju; intelektualno obrazovanje i duhovni život trebaju se uzajamno podupirati.
magisterium.assessment_en: The description of a personal vow and serious study of theology is in accordance with the Catholic understanding of faith as a call to respond to God, and in the passage there is no obvious contradiction of Catholic teaching. From the clip itself, however, it is not possible to assess the nature or binding force of the vow in this specific case.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic tradition values theological study because it helps to understand the entirety of faith and give reason for Christian hope, rather than merely acquiring practical knowledge. At the same time, the study of theology must remain connected with prayer, humility, and love; intellectual education and spiritual life should mutually support one another.

sections.subtitle_en: A vow fulfilled at the age of 60: from “theology on one's knees” to a degree
sections.screenshot_description_en: Dario Kordić speaks about his vow to enroll in the study of theology if he gets out of prison
sections.content_en:
Krunoslav observes that during those 17 years Kordić was actually “studying theology on his knees”, yet in the same year he got out he also enrolled in formal theology studies. He asks whether that was a vow.

Kordić confirms that it was. When he felt a spiritual calling in prison, he promised the Lord: if he had the opportunity to live outside prison walls, he would enroll in those studies. He adds jokingly that he did not do it because he had nothing else to do.

He was, he says, **a zealous student**. In five years of study he missed only two days, due to funerals. He did not seek any exemptions: he attended physical education, and visits, and everything else that other students had. He enjoyed his studies and discovered in them many things he had not known before.

Some people teased him that he would “lose his faith in theology studies”. Kordić replies that, thank God, there he only **deepened** it. He graduated during the time of corona, surrounded by many young people. He finished his first university degree in 1983, sat at student desks again after 31 years, and finished his second university degree **in the 60th year of his life**.

sections.subtitle: Javna molitva krunice i molitva za one s druge strane ograde
sections.screenshot_description: Dario Kordić govori o molitvi za prosvjednike tijekom javne muške molitve krunice
sections.content:
Nekoliko godina nakon povratka pokrenuta je **javna molitva krunice muškaraca**, a Kordić se među prvima pridružio. Krunoslav ga pita kako se kao javna osoba nosi s pozornošću medija, koji su ga, kaže voditelj, odmah „uočili i ulovili“.

Kordić kaže da je o tome često razgovarao sa suprugom i da su oboje bili istog mišljenja: on **ne bježi ni od koga**. Pojavit će se gdje treba, a nikome ne želi stvarati probleme. Molitvu je doživio kao „**Božji projekt**“ u kojem se muškarci, inače rijetko okupljeni u tolikom broju, okupljaju oko plemenite, duhovne misije.

Sjeća se prvih molitava, dok se još nije molilo na strani trga prema Franku, kad nije bilo ni banera ni toliko policije, a ni prosvjeda. Nije dolazio na svaku molitvu, ali bio je tri do četiri puta godišnje. Mediji su ga, kaže, primijetili jedno dvaput, a poslije im valjda više nije bilo zanimljivo pa su ga pustili na miru.

Isposlovaje da je, ponekad i predvodeći molitvu na mikrofonu, mnogo puta molio i **za prosvjednike**, da osjete Božju ljubav: „Evo, Gospodine, daj njih dotakni, pa da možda netko od njih dođe ovamo, pa da posvjedoči da je bio s one strane.“ Uvjeren je da bi takav čovjek bio prihvaćen s ljubavlju, jer „ima mjesta u Božjoj kući za svih“.

Krunoslav se nadovezuje pričom o jednom molitelju s trga koji kaže da je prosvjednika „premalo“. Volio bi da ih je što više, kako bi se što više njih obratilo od silnih molitava *Zdravo Marijo*. Kordić smatra da se obraćenja doista i događaju.

magisterium.assessment: Javna molitva krunice i spremnost na nenametljivo javno svjedočenje vjere u skladu su s katoličkom pobožnošću; krunica je kristološka molitva koja se može moliti osobno i zajednički. Iz dostupnog ulomka ne vidi se tvrdnja protivna nauku, ali izraz „Božji projekt” ostaje osobno tumačenje koje samo po sebi ne dokazuje da je riječ o posebnom Božjem nalogu.
concerns: Budući da je ulomak prekinut, ne može se procijeniti što se točno podrazumijeva pod molitvom za „one s druge strane ograde”; važno je da se ona usmjerava prema njihovu dobru, a ne prema ponižavanju ili neprijateljstvu.
Izraz „Božji projekt” prikladno je razumjeti kao osobno razlučivanje, a ne kao tvrdnju o nedvojbenoj Božjoj objavi ili posebnom poslanju.
magisterium.enrichment: Sveti Ivan Pavao II. opisuje krunicu kao molitvu u kojoj se Kristova otajstva promatraju Marijinim očima, a potiče i na osobnu i zajedničku molitvu krunice. Javno moljenje može biti svjedočanstvo vjere, ali kršćanska molitva uključuje i prošnju za druge: biblijski poticaj koji navodi Ivan Pavao II. obuhvaća molitve za sve ljude, a ne samo za vlastitu zajednicu.

magisterium.assessment_en: The public prayer of the Rosary and the readiness for an unobtrusive public witness of faith are in accordance with Catholic piety; the Rosary is a Christological prayer that can be prayed personally and communally. From the available excerpt, no assertion contrary to doctrine is evident, but the phrase "God's project" remains a personal interpretation that does not in itself prove it is a matter of a special divine mandate.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Saint John Paul II describes the Rosary as a prayer in which the mysteries of Christ are contemplated through Mary's eyes, and he encourages both personal and communal recitation of the Rosary. Public prayer can be a witness of faith, but Christian prayer also includes supplication for others: the biblical encouragement cited by John Paul II encompasses prayers for all people, and not only for one's own community.
concerns_en: Since the excerpt is truncated, it cannot be evaluated what exactly is meant by praying for "those on the other side of the fence"; it is important that it be directed toward their good, rather than toward humiliation or hostility.
It is appropriate to understand the phrase "God's project" as personal discernment, rather than as an assertion of unmistakable divine revelation or a special mission.

sections.subtitle_en: Public Rosary prayer and prayer for those on the other side of the fence
sections.screenshot_description_en: Dario Kordić speaks about praying for protesters during the public men's Rosary prayer
sections.content_en:
A few years after the return, the **public men's Rosary prayer** was launched, and Kordić was among the first to join. Krunoslav asks him how, as a public figure, he deals with the attention of the media, who, says the host, immediately "spotted and caught" him.

Kordić says that he often spoke about this with his wife and that they were both of the same opinion: he **does not run away from anyone**. He will appear where he needs to, and he does not want to create problems for anyone. He experienced the prayer as "**God's project**" in which men, otherwise rarely gathered in such numbers, gather around a noble, spiritual mission.

He remembers the first prayers, when they did not yet pray on the side of the square toward Frank, when there were neither banners nor so much police, nor protests. He did not come to every prayer, but he attended three to four times a year. The media, he says, noticed him once or twice, and later it was probably no longer interesting to them, so they left him alone.

He recounts that, sometimes even leading the prayer on the microphone, he prayed many times **for the protesters** as well, that they might feel God's love: "Here, Lord, touch them, so that perhaps someone among them might come over here, and testify that he was on that side." He is convinced that such a person would be welcomed with love, because "there is room in God's house for all."

Krunoslav follows up with a story about a person praying from the square who says there are "too few" protesters. He would like there to be as many of them as possible, so that as many of them as possible would convert from the powerful *Hail Mary* prayers. Kordić believes that conversions truly do happen.

sections.subtitle: Branitelji ispod mostova: pola tjedna za one koje je društvo zaboravilo
sections.screenshot_description: Dario Kordić opisuje hrvatske branitelje koji spavaju na kolodvorima i ispod mostova
sections.content:
Kordić otkriva da se posljednjih četiri do pet godina ponajviše posvećuje **braniteljskoj populaciji**. Zajedno s bratom **Marinkom Šuškom**, u okviru **Mreže instituta** i s paterom **Mikom Mandurićem**, pokrenuo je inicijativu kojoj je cilj doći do hrvatskih branitelja **na rubu društva**. To su, kaže, ljudi koji „večeras spavaju na kolodvorima, na klupama, ispod mostova, u šupama“.

Razloga za takvu sudbinu ima, prema njegovim riječima, stotinu. Neki su nekad imali riješenu egzistenciju, drugi je nikad nisu imali. Zajedničko im je da trebaju **pruženu ruku** i nekoga tko će ih pokušati izvući uz Božju pomoć.

Aktivnosti uključuju:
- **duhovne obnove na Pašmanu**, u starom franjevačkom samostanu s paterom Mikom, koje traju već tri do četiri godine;
- obnove s **Kursiljom** i **Andrijom Vranom** na **Krapnju**, na koje dolaze i hrvatski branitelji;
- obilaske po cijeloj Hrvatskoj, od **Banovine i Slavonije** do **Dalmacije i Rijeke**, dok se mreža kontakata stalno širi.

Kordić procjenjuje da otprilike **pola svakog tjedna**, uz vrijeme za obitelj i unuke, posvećuje pomaganju braniteljima. Kaže da je u tome posebno sretan i da to ne doživljava samo kao ljubav, nego i kao svakodnevno suočavanje s konkretnim problemima za koje pokušava naći rješenja.

### Udruga Brat branitelj

Na Krunoslavovo pitanje Kordić potvrđuje da je riječ o **Udruzi Brat branitelj**, koja postoji otprilike godinu i pet mjeseci. Udruga surađuje s **Ministarstvom branitelja**, bez kojeg neke stvari nije moguće riješiti. Kordić priznaje da su u ministarstvu za svakoga za koga su došli pitati nastojali pomoći. „Istina što je istina, ja ću je reći“, kaže, dodajući da je nebitno što za vlastiti slučaj nekad nije naišao na razumijevanje, jer su važnija pitanja šire naravi.

magisterium.assessment: Prikaz skrbi za branitelje koji žive na ulici ili na društvenoj margini u skladu je s katoličkim naukom o dostojanstvu svake osobe i pozivu na konkretnu ljubav prema potrebitima. Odlomak ne iznosi teološki sporne tvrdnje; opisuje inicijativu solidarnosti, premda je dostupni tekst prekinut prije dovršetka misli.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko razumijevanje takve skrbi ne svodi se na sažaljenje: u osobi koja spava na otvorenom kršćanin je pozvan prepoznati čovjeka jednake dostojanstvenosti, ljubljenoga od Boga i brata ili sestru otkupljene Kristom. Isusovo poistovjećivanje s najmanjima u Mateju 25 daje djelima milosrđa snažno evanđeosko značenje, a crkveno načelo prvenstvene brige za siromašne podrazumijeva i praktičnu pomoć te obranu njihova dostojanstva.

magisterium.assessment_en: The presentation of care for veterans living on the street or on the margins of society is in accordance with Catholic teaching on the dignity of every person and the call to concrete love toward those in need. The passage does not make theologically disputed claims; it describes an initiative of solidarity, although the available text is interrupted before completing the thought.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic understanding of such care is not reduced to pity: in a person sleeping in the open, a Christian is called to recognize a human being of equal dignity, loved by God, and a brother or sister redeemed by Christ. Jesus' identification with the least in Matthew 25 gives works of mercy a powerful evangelical meaning, and the Church's principle of preferential care for the poor implies both practical help and the defense of their dignity.

sections.subtitle_en: Veterans under bridges: half a week for those forgotten by society
sections.screenshot_description_en: Dario Kordić describes Croatian veterans sleeping at train stations and under bridges
sections.content_en:
Kordić reveals that over the past four to five years he has mostly dedicated himself to the **veteran population**. Together with his brother **Marinko Šušak**, within the framework of **Mreža instituta** and with Father **Miko Mandurić**, he launched an initiative whose goal is to reach Croatian veterans **on the margins of society**. These are, he says, people who "tonight sleep at train stations, on benches, under bridges, in sheds."

There are, according to his words, a hundred reasons for such a fate. Some once had a settled livelihood, others never had it. What they have in common is that they need **an outstretched hand** and someone who will try to pull them out with God's help.

Activities include:
- **spiritual retreats on Pašman**, in an old Franciscan monastery with Father Miko, which have been going on for three to four years now;
- retreats with **Kursiljo** and **Andrija Vrana** on **Krapanj**, which are also attended by Croatian veterans;
- visits throughout all of Croatia, from **Banovina and Slavonija** to **Dalmacija and Rijeka**, while the network of contacts constantly expands.

Kordić estimates that he dedicates roughly **half of each week**, alongside time for family and grandchildren, to helping veterans. He says that he is particularly happy in this and that he experiences it not only as love, but also as a daily confrontation with concrete problems for which he tries to find solutions.

### Udruga Brat branitelj

To Krunoslav's question, Kordić confirms that it is about **Udruga Brat branitelj**, which has existed for about a year and five months. The association collaborates with the **Ministarstvo branitelja**, without which some things cannot be resolved. Kordić acknowledges that at the ministry they strove to help everyone they came to inquire about. "Truth is truth, I will say it," he says, adding that it is irrelevant that for his own case he did not once find understanding, because broader questions are more important.
keywords_en: veterans on the margins of society

sections.subtitle: „Ponovio bih“: što je Kordić zapravo rekao i zašto je i dalje na američkoj crnoj listi
sections.screenshot_description: Dario Kordić objašnjava pravo značenje izjave „vrijedilo je, ponovio bih“
sections.content:
Krunoslav otvara osjetljivu temu. Prije nekoliko godina objavljen je novinski naslov prema kojem je Kordić navodno rekao da bi „sve ponovio“, a ta mu je rečenica „prišivena“ u kontekstu **Ahmića**. Voditelj ga moli da pojasni što je zapravo mislio.

Kordić najprije ironično primjećuje da mediji „bolje znaju što ja u srcu nosim nego ja“, dok srce svakoga čovjeka, kaže, zna samo Bog. Zatim objašnjava kontekst. Bio je upitan je li vrijedilo rata, zatvora i svih žrtava. Odgovorio je: „Vrijedilo je, **ponovio bih**, svaka je sekunda vrijedila.“ Smisao izjave, kaže, bio je osobni i duhovni: da nije prošao zatočeništvo, ne bi na takav način susreo Isusa Krista i bio bi „siromašan čovjek“.

### Na listi s Bin Ladenom

Istu je poruku, otkriva Kordić, uputio i jednoj **američkoj agenciji** koja prati rehabilitaciju bivših osuđenika. Ta ga agencija, kako navodi, i dalje drži na **crnoj listi**, zajedno s **Bin Ladenom** i sličnima. Godine **2017.** poslao im je dopis u kojem je naveo da studira teologiju i da nikome ne stvara probleme. Zamolio je da ga skinu s liste jer zbog nje, kaže, ne može normalno plaćati plin i struju, poslovati s bankom ni uopće funkcionirati.

Na odgovor je čekao **osam godina**. Stigao je prije otprilike pola godine do godine dana, a u njemu su ga pitali upravo kako može tvrditi da se rehabilitirao kad je izjavio da bi „ponovio“. Kordić im je odgovorio istim riječima kao i u podcastu: vrijedilo je sve što je prošao, jer bez toga ne bi susreo živoga Boga.

magisterium.assessment: Prema dostupnom ulomku, Kordić osporava medijsko pripisivanje izjave i priznaje da samo Bog poznaje ljudsko srce; to je samo po sebi spojivo s kršćanskom suzdržanošću u prosudbi tuđih motiva. Budući da je odlomak prekinut nakon riječi „Vrijedilo je,...”, nije moguće utvrditi odnosi li se nastavak na osobnu žrtvu ili na opravdavanje rata i zločina.
concerns: Ako bi nastavak značio da su zločin u Ahmićima, ubijanje nevinih ili žrtve rata bili vrijedni ili da bi ih trebalo ponoviti, takvo bi opravdavanje bilo ozbiljno nespojivo s kršćanskim poštovanjem ljudskog života i moralnom odgovornošću.
Bez cjelovite izjave ne može se pouzdano zaključiti što je govornik mislio ni ocijeniti točnu tvrdnju.
magisterium.enrichment: Kršćanska procjena rata ne smije se svesti na usporedbu s neprijateljevim grijesima, nego mora gledati pravednost pred Bogom i vlastitu odgovornost; Fulton Sheen izričito upozorava na takvo samopravdanje. Ivan Pavao II. naglašava da su u ratovima na Balkanu većinu žrtava činili nevini te razlikuje njihovu sudbinu od odgovornosti onih koji su vodili operacije. Zato je nužno razlučiti žaljenje zbog stradanja, prosudbu povijesnih okolnosti i opravdavanje konkretnog zločina.
magisterium.assessment_en: According to the available excerpt, Kordić disputes the media's attribution of the statement and acknowledges that only God knows the human heart; this is in itself compatible with Christian restraint in judging others' motives. Since the paragraph was cut off after the words "It was worth it,...", it is not possible to determine whether the continuation refers to personal sacrifice or to the justification of war and crimes.
magisterium.enrichment_en: A Christian assessment of war must not be reduced to a comparison with the enemy's sins, but must look at righteousness before God and one's own responsibility; Fulton Sheen explicitly warns against such self-justification. John Paul II emphasizes that in the wars in the Balkans, the majority of victims were innocent and distinguishes their fate from the responsibility of those who led operations. Therefore, it is necessary to distinguish sorrow over suffering, judgment of historical circumstances, and justification of a concrete crime.
concerns_en: If the continuation were to mean that the crime in Ahmići, the killing of innocents, or the casualties of war were worth it or should be repeated, such justification would be seriously incompatible with Christian respect for human life and moral responsibility.
Without the complete statement, one cannot reliably conclude what the speaker meant or evaluate the precise claim.

sections.subtitle_en: "I would repeat it": what Kordić actually said and why he is still on the American blacklist
sections.screenshot_description_en: Dario Kordić explains the true meaning of the statement "it was worth it, I would repeat it"
sections.content_en:
Krunoslav opens a sensitive topic. Several years ago, a newspaper headline was published according to which Kordić allegedly said that he "would repeat everything," and that sentence was "pinned" on him in the context of **Ahmići**. The host asks him to clarify what he actually meant.

Kordić first ironically notes that the media "know better what I carry in my heart than I do," while the heart of every person, he says, is known only to God. Then he explains the context. He was asked whether the war, imprisonment, and all the sacrifices were worth it. He replied: "It was worth it, **I would repeat it**, every second was worth it." The meaning of the statement, he says, was personal and spiritual: if he had not gone through captivity, he would not have encountered Jesus Christ in such a way and would be a "poor man."

### On the list with Bin Laden

Kordić reveals that he sent the same message to an **American agency** that monitors the rehabilitation of former convicts. That agency, as he states, still keeps him on the **blacklist**, together with **Bin Laden** and the like. In **2017**, he sent them a letter stating that he was studying theology and causing problems for no one. He asked them to remove him from the list because, due to it, he says, he cannot normally pay for gas and electricity, do business with a bank, or function at all.

He waited **eight years** for an answer. It arrived about half a year to a year ago, and in it they asked him specifically how he could claim to be rehabilitated when he stated that he would "repeat it." Kordić answered them with the same words as in the podcast: everything he went through was worth it, because without it he would not have encountered the living God.

sections.subtitle: Tri medijska nastupa u dvanaest godina i isprika nakon Pompejske pobožnosti
sections.screenshot_description: Dario Kordić govori o suprugi koja je molila za klevetnike i o primljenoj isprici
sections.content:
Kordić naglašava da do ovog podcasta nikada nije javno demantirao napise o sebi. Ovo mu je tek **treći medijski nastup u dvanaest godina** na slobodi:
- prvi je bio na jednoj svjetovnoj televiziji kod urednice **Ozane**, gdje se razgovaralo o općim temama, a on je u studio donio križ i krunicu pa je emisija, kako kaže, ispala duhovna;
- drugi je bio prije otprilike godinu i pol kod patera **Ike** u **Magis institutu**;
- treći je ovaj podcast.

Obitelj Kordić, ističe, u **33 godine** nije odgovorila ni na jednu objedu ni laž. Sve nose strpljivo. Ako ne dobiju barem četiri do pet napada godišnje, on se, kaže, zabrine.

### „Molim se za ljude koji ovo pljuju“

U vrijeme najžešćih napada pater Ike pozvao je supružnike na razgovor i molitvu. Kordić napominje da tada još nije redovito molio s njim, a sada ondje ima termin četvrtkom u molitvi „**Krunica Hrvata svega svijeta**“. Venera je tom prilikom rekla: „Pater Ike, ja se molim za ljude koji ovo pljuju, da im Gospodin dotakne njihovo srce.“

Kordić priznaje da se za neke ljude čini kako ne vrijedi ni moliti, no pokazalo se drukčije. Supruga je molila **Pompejsku pobožnost**: 27 dana krunice na nakanu i 27 dana zahvale. Predzadnjeg dana Kordiću je stigla poruka preko prijatelja koji je nekoć bio visoko pozicioniran, „najviše u Bosni i Hercegovini u svoja vremena“. Poruku je slao čovjek koji ga je na jednom portalu godinama ponajviše napadao. Pitao je može li mu Kordić oprostiti što ga je dvanaest godina tako blatio, jer je u međuvremenu proučio neke stvari i postalo ga je sram.

Kordić mu je poslao oprost i zaključuje: „Supruga je to izmolila. Znači, **nema izgubljenih slučajeva**.“

magisterium.assessment: Opis šutnje pred osobnim objavama, oprosta i molitve za neprijatelje uglavnom je u skladu s kršćanskim naukom: Evanđelje poziva na prekid osvete i na molitvu za one koji nam čine zlo. Ipak, šutnja nije obvezna u svakoj situaciji niti sama po sebi dokazuje nevinost; iz dostavljenog sažetka ne može se procijeniti što je točno rečeno u isprici ni njezine okolnosti.
concerns: Ako bi se tvrdnja o nedemantiranju napisa tumačila kao opća dužnost da se o nepravdi uvijek šuti, to bi bilo pretjerano: katolička poniznost i blagost mogu uključivati i mirno traženje pravde ili obranu slabijih. Dostavljeni tekst, međutim, ne kaže da Kordić takvu šutnju propisuje svima.
Odlomak je prekinut nakon riječi „Obitelj Kordić...“, pa se ne mogu pouzdano ocijeniti cijeli kontekst ni konkretan sadržaj spomenute isprike.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički nauk razlikuje oprost od poricanja nepravde: kršćanin je pozvan ne uzvraćati zlom za zlo i moliti za neprijatelje, ali može blago i bez osvete iznijeti istinu, tražiti pravdu ili braniti drugoga. Krunica i pompejska pobožnost mogu biti izrazi marijanske molitve koja vodi Kristu; crkveno tumačenje Krunice naglašava njezinu usmjerenost na Isusove otajstva te poticaj na mir, a ne na osvetu.

citations.document_title: Letter 84 - To Pammachius And Oceanus (Eusebius Sophronius Hieronymus (Jerome of Stridon or St. Jerome))
19 October 2008: Holy Mass in the square in front of the Pontifical Shrine of Pompeii

magisterium.assessment_en: The description of silence in the face of personal publications, forgiveness, and prayer for enemies is largely in accordance with Christian teaching: the Gospel calls for an end to vengeance and for prayer for those who do us harm. However, silence is not mandatory in every situation nor does it in itself prove innocence; from the provided summary, it cannot be assessed what exactly was said in the apology or its circumstances.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic teaching distinguishes forgiveness from denying injustice: the Christian is called not to repay evil for evil and to pray for enemies, but may gently and without vengeance present the truth, seek justice, or defend another. The Rosary and the Pompeian devotion can be expressions of Marian prayer that leads to Christ; the Church's interpretation of the Rosary emphasizes its focus on the mysteries of Jesus and the call to peace, rather than vengeance.
concerns_en: If the claim about not denying writings were interpreted as a general duty to always remain silent about injustice, that would be exaggerated: Catholic humility and gentleness can also include peacefully seeking justice or defending the weaker. The provided text, however, does not say that Kordić prescribes such silence to everyone.
The excerpt was interrupted after the words „Obitelj Kordić...“, so the entire context and the specific content of the mentioned apology cannot be reliably assessed.

sections.subtitle_en: Three media appearances in twelve years and an apology after the Pompeian devotion
sections.screenshot_description_en: Dario Kordić speaks about his wife who prayed for slanderers and about the apology received
sections.content_en:
Kordić emphasizes that until this podcast he had never publicly denied writings about himself. This is only his **third media appearance in twelve years** of freedom:
- the first was on a secular television station with editor **Ozana**, where general topics were discussed, and he brought a cross and a Rosary into the studio so the show, as he says, turned out spiritual;
- the second was about a year and a half ago with pater **Ike** at the **Magis institut**;
- the third is this podcast.

The Kordić family, he points out, in **33 years** has not responded to a single slander or lie. They bear everything patiently. If they do not receive at least four to five attacks a year, he says, he gets worried.

### „Molim se za ljude koji ovo pljuju“

At the time of the fiercest attacks, pater Ike invited the spouses for a conversation and prayer. Kordić notes that back then he was not yet regularly praying with him, and now he has a slot there on Thursdays in the prayer „**Krunica Hrvata svega svijeta**“. Venera on that occasion said: „Pater Ike, I pray for the people who spit on this, that the Lord may touch their heart.“

Kordić admits that for some people it seems not even worth praying, but it turned out differently. His wife prayed the **Pompeian devotion**: 27 days of the Rosary for an intention and 27 days of thanksgiving. On the penultimate day, a message reached Kordić through a friend who was once highly positioned, „the highest in Bosna i Hercegovina in his time“. The message was sent by a man who on one portal had attacked him the most for years. He asked whether Kordić could forgive him for slandering him like that for twelve years, because in the meantime he had studied some things and became ashamed.

Kordić sent him forgiveness and concludes: „My wife prayed this through. That means, **there are no lost causes**.“
keywords_en: silence in the face of slanders

sections.subtitle: „Hrvatska s Kristom“ i blic pitanja: križ, zavičaj, sveci i Međugorje
sections.screenshot_description: Dario Kordić odgovara na blic pitanja voditelja Krunoslava
sections.content:
Na kraju razgovora Krunoslav traži od gosta poruku. Kordić se obraća Hrvatima koji gledaju podcast:

> „Ukoliko smo s Kristom kao Hrvatska, ne trebamo ništa dvojiti, bojati se, samo budimo s Kristom, sve će onda biti i Hrvatska će biti na mjestu. Ukoliko mi nismo s Kristom, onda bilo što oko nas može biti najljepše, to nema vrijednosti.“

Uslijedila su **blic pitanja** s dvije ponuđene opcije, za koja voditelj unaprijed napominje da su „malo provokativna, malo zeznuta“.

**Krunica u ruci ili križ oko vrata?** Kordić bira **križ**. Ljubi ga jer mu je Gospodin pokazao da bez križa nema vječnoga života, a zahvaljivao je, kaže, na svim križevima.

**Busovača ili Zagreb?** Odgovara „**i jedno i drugo**“. Zavičaj, Žepče i Busovača, uvijek je u srcu, ali svaki dio Hrvatske doživljava kao svoj i nema sela u kojem ne osjeti radost. Posebno spominje **svetog Antu Padovanskog**, zaštitnika Busovače, i kip **Kuzme Kovačića** koji je četiri godine nakon rata imao priliku vidjeti.

**Sveti Ante ili Gospa?** Kordić izabire **Gospu**, ali dodaje da je na prvom mjestu **Krist**, a tek kroz Krista sveti Ante i Gospa. Prije je bio posebno vezan uz svetog Antu, no otkad je s obitelji u župi **svetog Josipa na Trešnjevci**, upoznao je, kaže, milosti koje se mogu izmoliti po svetom Josipu, „toliko moćnom svecu koji je Krista odgajao“. Krunoslav dodaje da se u to svatko mora sam uvjeriti.

**Mariazell ili Međugorje?** Kordić bira **Međugorje**. Ističe da nismo svjesni kolika je milost kroz Međugorje došla cijelom svijetu i da je **Međugorska Majka** njega osobno snažno pratila. Kad Krunoslav primijeti da se Gospa „ukazala kao Hercegovka“, Kordić to potvrđuje, ali upozorava da Hrvati zbog toga ne smiju biti „bahati“, jer je riječ o milosti koja se „ne može riječima opisati“.

magisterium.assessment: Poziv da se osobno i zajednički živi s Kristom u skladu je s kršćanskim središtem vjere, ali tvrdnja da će „sve onda biti” i da će Hrvatska „biti na mjestu” može zvučati kao obećanje da će vjernost Kristu automatski donijeti nacionalni uspjeh ili povoljne okolnosti. Budući da je odlomak prekinut prije sadržaja blic-pitanja, o njima se ne može dati pouzdana teološka procjena.
concerns: Nejasno je znači li „sve će onda biti” duhovno pouzdanje u Krista ili obećanje zemaljskog blagostanja i političke stabilnosti; potonje se ne bi smjelo prikazivati kao zajamčena posljedica vjere.

Izraz „s Kristom kao Hrvatska” može se razumjeti kao poziv narodu na kršćanski život, ali treba izbjeći poistovjećivanje vjere u Krista s nacionalnom pripadnošću ili tvrdnju da je vrijednost Hrvatske uvjetovana jednom političkom ili nacionalnom predodžbom.
magisterium.enrichment: Kršćanska poruka opravdano stavlja Krista u središte: križ je za one koji se spašavaju „snaga Božja”, a ne obećanje života bez kušnji ili društvenih teškoća. Zajedničko kršćansko nasljeđe može biti važan dio povijesti naroda, ali poziv na vjernost Kristu najbolje se razumije kao poziv na obraćenje, pravednost i ljubav, a ne kao jamstvo nacionalnog blagostanja. U dostavljenom tekstu nema dovoljno sadržaja za procjenu navedenih tema o svecima, križu ili Međugorju.
magisterium.assessment_en: The call to live personally and communally with Christ is in accordance with the Christian center of faith, but the claim that "everything will then be fine" and that Croatia will "be in its place" may sound like a promise that faithfulness to Christ will automatically bring national success or favorable circumstances. Since the excerpt was cut off before the content of the blitz questions, a reliable theological assessment cannot be given regarding them.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Christian message rightly places Christ at the center: for those who are being saved, the cross is the "power of God," not a promise of a life without trials or social difficulties. A shared Christian heritage can be an important part of a nation's history, but the call to faithfulness to Christ is best understood as a call to conversion, justice, and love, not as a guarantee of national prosperity. In the submitted text, there is not enough content to evaluate the mentioned topics about the saints, the cross, or Međugorje.
concerns_en: It is unclear whether "everything will then be fine" means spiritual trust in Christ or a promise of earthly prosperity and political stability; the latter should not be presented as a guaranteed consequence of faith.

The expression "with Christ as Croatia" can be understood as a call to the nation to a Christian life, but one should avoid equating faith in Christ with national belonging or claiming that the value of Croatia is conditioned by a single political or national conception.

sections.subtitle_en: "Croatia with Christ" and blitz questions: the cross, homeland, saints, and Međugorje
sections.screenshot_description_en: Dario Kordić answers host Krunoslav's blitz questions
sections.content_en:
At the end of the conversation, Krunoslav asks the guest for a message. Kordić addresses the Croats watching the podcast:

> "If we are with Christ as Croatia, we do not need to doubt anything, to fear; let us just be with Christ, everything will then be fine and Croatia will be in its place. If we are not with Christ, then whatever is around us may be the most beautiful, it has no value."

There followed **blitz questions** with two offered options, which the host notes in advance are "a little provocative, a little tricky."

**A Rosary in hand or a cross around the neck?** Kordić chooses the **cross**. He kisses it because the Lord showed him that without the cross there is no eternal life, and he gave thanks, he says, for all crosses.

**Busovača or Zagreb?** He answers "**both**." The homeland, Žepče and Busovača, is always in the heart, but he experiences every part of Croatia as his own and there is no village in which he does not feel joy. He specifically mentions **Saint Anthony of Padua**, the patron of Busovača, and the statue by **Kuzma Kovačić** which he had the opportunity to see four years after the war.

**Saint Anthony or Our Lady?** Kordić chooses **Our Lady**, but adds that in the first place is **Christ**, and only through Christ Saint Anthony and Our Lady. Previously, he was especially attached to Saint Anthony, but since he has been with his family in the parish of **Saint Joseph in Trešnjevka**, he has come to know, he says, the graces that can be obtained through prayer to Saint Joseph, "such a powerful saint who raised Christ." Krunoslav adds that everyone must be convinced of this for themselves.

**Mariazell or Međugorje?** Kordić chooses **Međugorje**. He emphasizes that we are not aware of how much grace has come to the whole world through Međugorje and that the **Mother of Međugorje** has personally accompanied him strongly. When Krunoslav remarks that Our Lady "appeared as a woman of Herzegovina," Kordić confirms this, but warns that Croats must not be "arrogant" because of that, because it is a grace that "cannot be described in words."

sections.subtitle: Zahvale na kraju i najava: molitva umjesto osvete
sections.screenshot_description: Gost sljedeće epizode u najavi govori o napadu i molitvi za napadača
sections.content:
Krunoslav zahvaljuje „dragom bratu“ na gostovanju i izražava uvjerenje da je Kordićevo svjedočanstvo mnogima progovorilo, potaknulo ih na razmišljanje i možda promijenilo sliku koju su o njemu imali. Kordić uzvraća zahvalom Gospodinu na tom danu i emisiji, uz želju da „dotakne mnoga srca“, te zahvaljuje voditelju što je razgovor vodio „u Duhu Svetom“.

Voditelj zatim poziva gledatelje da podrže podcast **Redefinicija** lajkanjem, dijeljenjem, pretplatom na YouTube kanal te novčano i molitveno. Napominje da se sljedeća epizoda može pogledati odmah putem profila na **Patreonu**, bez čekanja mjesec dana.

### Najava sljedeće epizode

U kratkom isječku **gost sljedeće epizode** prepričava kako je napadnut na javnom mjestu, nakon čega je policija obavila očevid. Umjesto uzvraćanja on i njegovi bližnji odlučili su **moliti za napadača**. To naziva „poantom Božje pedagogije“: nisu išli „na mišiće“, nego „na Božji način“. Nakon nekog vremena napadač je uplatio prilog župniku za crkvu, nazvao ga telefonom i zamolio za oprost. Najava se tako tematski nadovezuje na poruku kojom je Kordić zaključio svoje svjedočanstvo: da nema izgubljenih slučajeva.

magisterium.assessment: Zahvaljivanje Bogu, želja da razgovor dotakne ljude te poziv na molitvenu i materijalnu potporu sami po sebi su u skladu s katoličkom zahvalnošću i zajedničkim apostolskim djelovanjem. Izraz da je voditelj razgovor vodio „u Duhu Svetom” može se razumjeti kao osobno svjedočanstvo i zahvalnost, a ne kao tvrdnja da je emisija nepogrešiva ili službeno potvrđena od Crkve.
magisterium.enrichment: Kršćanska zahvalnost nije samo pristojna završna riječ: ona je odgovor na Božje darove i usmjerava čovjeka prema živom odnosu s Bogom. Spominjanje Duha Svetoga može izraziti vjeru da Duh djeluje u ljudima i pomaže djelu spasenja, ali takvo osobno razlučivanje ne znači da je svaka izrečena tvrdnja ili sadržaj automatski zajamčen Božjim autoritetom.
magisterium.assessment_en: Giving thanks to God, the desire for the conversation to touch people, and the call for prayerful and material support are in themselves in accordance with Catholic gratitude and shared apostolic activity. The expression that the host led the conversation "in the Holy Spirit" can be understood as personal testimony and gratitude, rather than as a claim that the show is infallible or officially confirmed by the Church.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Christian gratitude is not merely a polite concluding word: it is a response to God's gifts and directs man toward a living relationship with God. Mentioning the Holy Spirit can express faith that the Spirit works in people and aids the work of salvation, but such personal discernment does not mean that every uttered statement or content is automatically guaranteed by divine authority.

sections.subtitle_en: Thanks at the end and announcement: prayer instead of revenge
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest of the next episode speaks in the preview about an attack and prayer for the attacker
sections.content_en:
Krunoslav thanks the "dear brother" for his guest appearance and expresses his conviction that Kordić's testimony spoke to many, prompted them to reflect, and perhaps changed the image they had of him. Kordić responds by thanking the Lord for that day and the show, with the wish that it "touch many hearts", and thanks the host for leading the conversation "in the Holy Spirit".

The host then invites viewers to support the podcast **Redefinicija** by liking, sharing, subscribing to the YouTube channel, and financially and prayerfully. He notes that the next episode can be watched immediately through the profile on **Patreon**, without waiting a month.

### Announcement of the next episode

In a short clip, the **guest of the next episode** recounts how he was attacked in a public place, after which the police conducted an investigation. Instead of retaliating, he and those close to him decided to **pray for the attacker**. He calls this the "point of God's pedagogy": they did not go "by muscle", but "in God's way". After some time, the attacker made a donation to the parish priest for the church, called him by phone, and asked for forgiveness. The preview thus thematically connects to the message with which Kordić concluded his testimony: that there are no lost cases.
